News.title: El Chapo’s bloodthirsty cartel kingpin pal El Mayo gets life behind bars & will give up £11.2bn in drug profits
News.content:
A RUTHLESS cartel kingpin who reportedly skinned his victims and betrayed former pal El Chapo has been jailed for life.

Mexican druglord Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada spent four decades flooding the US with deadly drugs like heroin, cocaine and fentanyl and ordering gangsters to kill and torture anyone who stood in his way.



He ruled Mexico‘s most powerful drug trafficking syndicate – the Sinaloa Cartel – which he co-founded with notorious gangster Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán in the 1980s.

The kingpin had evaded arrest for decades – despite having a $15million bounty on his head.



The bloodthirsty criminal mastermind was captured in 2024 after El Chapo’s son tricked him into flying to Santa Teresa International Jetport in Texas – where he was met with law enforcement.

He entered a plea deal to spare himself from the death penalty last year – but in exchange will be forced to give up £11.2billion worth of drug profits.

Seven years ago his pal and cartel co-founder Joaquín “El Chapo” Guzmán was sentenced to life imprisonment after El Mayo told his incarcerated son to hand him in.

Now the same fate awaits Ismael “El Mayo” Zambada.

Speaking to Brooklyn Federal Court on July 20, the notorious cartel boss said he was sorry “for the harm I caused and for the example I set”.

He added, through a translator: “If there’s one thing I can say that has value today, it’s this: the violence must end.



“In Mexico and elsewhere affected by this type of crime, too many lives are lost, too many families are destroyed, and too many young people are trapped in a cycle that leads only to prison or death.”

His friend Guzmán was the flamboyant showman of the crime syndicate – while Zambada was the scheming strategist behind the vile network.

A suspected member of the cartel, Eladio, described his boss El Mayo as “more poisonous than a snake”.



The drug-dealing fiend plead guilty in August 2025 after prosecutors promised not to seek the death penalty.

Prosecutors said Zambada had been “one of the most – if not the most – prolific and powerful narcotraffickers in the world.

“It would be difficult to overstate the magnitude of his crimes and the scale of the corruption, violence, and other harm he spread throughout Mexico, the United States, and the world.”

Nearly half a million people died of fentanyl poisoning in the US last year, according to the government’s accountability office.

The cartel kingpin apologised “to everyone who has suffered or been affected by my actions” and admitted to transporting at least 1.5million kilograms of cocaine – most of which entered the United States.



The 76-year-old will now spend his life in a prison hospital because he suffers from a cocktail of “complex age-related health issues”, said his defence lawyer Frank Perez.

U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of New York Joseph Nocella, Jr. said: “Ismael Zambada Garcia spent nearly four decades poisoning American communities to make billions of dollars in profit and ordering the murders of anyone who stood in his way. Today, that chapter closes for good.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Though El Mayo will now rot behind bars, the deadly cartel he spawned with his associate El Chapo will continue, according to experts who spoke to CNN.

One suggested that the kingpin’s son Ismael “el Mayito Flaco” Zambada Sicairos may be crowned the new leader.

News.title: Granddad flung into air by 1-tonne bison speaks from hospital bed as x-rays show femur broken in 4 places
News.content:
A GRANDAD who was tossed like a rag doll by a bison in Yellowstone and had his bones shattered in multiple pieces has spoken out from his hospital bed.

Carl Isom-McDaniel, 65, was flung 8ft into the air by the animal – weighing one tonne – during a walk with his grandson at the National Park.



Footage shows the beast becoming agitated and charging at the man at full-speed, chasing him through the trees before it eventually hooked him with one of its horns and hurled him ahead.

McDaniel broke his femur, the strongest bone in the body, in four places near his hip.



An X-ray revealed the extent of what his doctor described as a “pretty painful injury.”

“We saw the bison and he was down,” McDaniel said from his hospital bed.

“He wasn’t showing signs of aggression… until it picked a target. That target happened to be me.

“At the time, I had my grandson with me… They move master that you ever imagine.



“He just kept coming and he was aggressive. And as soon as he got off that tree, he launched me in the air.

“I didn’t get bruises from him launching me in the air, but it was the landing that became the problem.”

McDaniel explained that his family had just finished eating dinner and he was out on a walk with his grandson when the attack took place.

He warned his grandson to get to safety and tried to run from the bison himself, but it continued to chase after him.

“Even though I was on the ground, he could’ve stomped me, he could’ve gored me, he could’ve done anything,” he added.



McDaniel said he is grateful to have survived the attack and believed his injuries could have been worse.

Pointing at the X-ray, his doctor explained that his bone is actually broken in “multiple pieces.”

“You can see some fragments here and there are fractures and break lines right through that,” he added.

Professional photographer Mike MacLeod captured the extraordinary incident on film, claiming that the victim was “in good spirits” as soon as the ordeal was over.

“He was in a lot of pain, but was conscious and joking the whole time,” he told Cowboy State Daily.



“He was really worried and wanted to see the video to make sure it wasn’t his fault.

“It’s not his fault. You can tell from the very beginning. That was a really, really angry bison.”

Prior to Carl’s near-death experience, the bison had already terrorised several other groups of visitors.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

In the aftermath, Yellowstone National Park told The Sun: “A 65-year-old man was injured by a bison on the evening of July 10 at Bridge Bay Campground near Lake Yellowstone in Yellowstone National Park.

“Park emergency medical personnel responded and transported him to a nearby hospital.”

News.title: Brit tourist, 60, drowns after being swept out to sea as his heartbroken family fume ‘lifeguards were slow to respond’
News.content:
OCEAN TRAGEDY Brit tourist, 60, drowns after being swept out to sea as his heartbroken family fume ‘lifeguards were slow to respond’

A BRITISH dad has drowned after being swept away to sea as his heartbroken family claim the lifeguards were too slow to respond.

The holidaymaker, 60, had been swimming in Cancun, Mexico with his two children when the tragedy unfolded.



Desperate onlookers began calling for help when they spotted the family battling the strong currents on Friday afternoon.

The area where the dad and his kids had entered opposite Nyx Hotel had been flying a red flag – a signal to swimmers for choppy seas.



The two youngsters, whose ages have not been revealed, were rescued alive.

But their father was hauled ashore unconscious – and later pronounced dead at the scene.



Devastated relatives accused the beach lifeguards of acting too slowly to rescue the Brit and his children, reported Mexican newspaper Por Esto.

They said that when they saw the father struggling in the water they begged a rescuer to intervene – but that their pleas were ignored.

It was only some moments later that a second lifeguard dove in to help the victims.

Officials have not yet made any comment about the alleged failings in the lifeguard service.



Police have launched an investigation into the incident.

The names of the father and his children have not yet been made public.

The popular tourist hotspot was cordoned off as ambulances and police swarmed the area.

Harrowing photos show the body lying on the beach covered by a blue blanket.

The beach where the British holidaymaker died is called San Miguelito Beach and is described as one of the best in Cancun.



One local insisted today: “Hoteles should warn guests about how dangerous going into the sea can be.”

Another said: “You come here on holiday and go home without your father. How sad.”

News.title: Britain is crying out for a leader, not a people-pleaser – Angry voters will be quick to punish Burnham if he fails
News.content:
No easy fixes

AFTER becoming our unelected Prime Minister yesterday, Andy Burnham said his generation of politicians needed to “raise our game”.

Unfortunately for the hard workers and wealth-creators of this country, one of his first acts might well be to raise their taxes.



The new PM yesterday repeated some of his high-spending vision: building tens of thousands of council houses, state control of energy and water and “re-industrialising” Britain using vast sums of taxpayers’ cash.

How he is going to pay for his ten-year plan — which, staggeringly, won’t be set out for months — remains to be seen.



Having celebrated in Downing Street with his Northern supporters, Burnham later refused to rule out increasing the top rate of income tax to 50p.

Despite that being a policy that has historically led to SMALLER tax receipts for the Treasury, he believes it could help pay for a lifting of thresholds for low-income taxpayers.

But experts reckon that could cost up to £5billion while delivering a saving to poorer workers of just £100 a year.

It falls to new Chancellor John Healey to make these difficult sums add up.

He must ensure the class-war politics of envy, which run deep in Burnham’s team — led by his de facto Deputy PM, the virulently left-wing Louise Haigh — don’t trump economic reality.

There will be widespread relief on the markets at Healey’s shock return to the Treasury at the expense of Ed Miliband, now made Foreign Secretary. It should also be good news for defence chiefs desperate for cash to re-arm.



But beyond the smiles and Manchester vibes, there are serious problems ahead.

The public have been clear for years about their priorities: cutting welfare, stopping the boats and fixing our broken borders system.

They are sick of paying sky-high taxes, believe Net Zero is failing and want more NEW drilling in the North Sea.

And they are fed up with political chaos delivering our seventh PM in just over a decade.

Has Burnham got the stomach to deliver any of this? More than half his party hates the idea of slashing welfare — the only way to find the money to mend our public services.



Instead, the fantasists on his backbenches want to soak the strivers with MORE tax to pay for reforms.

Meanwhile most Labour MPs want open borders and are hostile to Shabana Mahmood’s tough immigration reforms.

By purging almost every Starmer loyalist minister yesterday, Burnham may have also undermined his own promise to end infighting in the party.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Britain is crying out for a leader, not a people-pleaser.

Tinkering with bus fares and chucking £340million at ending rough sleeping is unlikely to cut it with angry voters, who will be quick to punish Burnham if he fails.

News.title: Andy Burnham launches brutal Cabinet bloodbath with Starmer allies purged as Rayner returns & Healey becomes Chancellor
News.content:
ANDY Burnham executed a brutal purge of Sir Keir Starmer’s Cabinet allies in his first move at No10.

The new Prime Minister shocked Westminster yesterday by revealing John Healey as his Chancellor after ­sacking Rachel Reeves.



Eco-crusading Ed Miliband had been gunning for the Treasury job — but was instead packed off abroad as Foreign Secretary.

Shabana Mahmood remained as Home Secretary to ­continue pushing through her immigration reforms.



Ms Reeves was one of the loyalists of outgoing PM Sir Keir Starmer who were pushed out as Mr Burnham cleared the decks on his first day in Downing Street.

Other casualties included David Lammy, Lord Hermer, Peter Kyle, Steve Reed, Liz Kendall, Nick Thomas-Symonds, Darren Jones, Jo ­Stevens and Hilary Benn.



They made way for Mr Burnham’s pals including comebacks for Angela Rayner and Louise Haigh — who were both forced to resign during Sir Keir’s tenure.

Ms Rayner, who quit in September over stamp duty on her flat in Hove, East Sussex, is back as Housing Secretary.



Ms Haigh departed in November 2024 after her fraud conviction was revealed.

She has now become Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster.

But the biggest surprise was the appointment of Mr Healey as Chancellor — only a month after he had quit as Defence Secretary in a dispute over military spending.



Downing Street sources said he was chosen as he shares Mr Burnham’s approach to the economy, combining fiscal discipline with investment to drive growth and regenerate industrial communities.

They also pointed to past ­Treasury experience under Gordon Brown when he was Chancellor, serving for five years as Economic Secretary and Financial Secretary.

Mr Healey said it was “time to get on with the job”.

He vowed to work in “lockstep” with Mr Burnham to meet strict fiscal rules and help in the cost-of-living fight.

Mr Healey added: “Fiscal control is the first duty of any Chancellor — it is mine — and fiscal credibility is the bedrock . . . for economic stability and for national security.



“You heard the Prime Minister this afternoon say, in this more dangerous world, we will meet our commitments on defence to our international allies.”

He now faces the task of finding the billions needed to deliver Mr Burnham’s defence promises without breaking Labour’s fiscal rules.

Late last night Wes Streeting was named Defence Secretary, succeeding Dan Jarvis who was in the role for less than six weeks.

Team Burnham was frustrated to discover that £4.7billion of the £15billion defence spending uplift was unfunded.

Yvette Cooper was demoted from Foreign Secretary to make way for Mr Miliband, becoming the Health Secretary instead.



Lucy Powell was made Education Secretary, with her divisive predecessor Bridget Phillipson demoted to keeping only part of her brief, remaining Minister for Women and Equalities.

Pat McFadden is staying as Welfare Secretary to sort out the crippling benefits bill, while Lisa Nandy stays as Culture Secretary.

Jonathan Reynolds returned to his old role as Business Secretary, and little-known Anneliese Midgley was named Chief Whip.

Ed Miliband’s protégée Miatta Fahnbulleh takes over from him as Energy Secretary.

Angela Eagle was named Environment Secretary and Alex Norris Justice Secretary.



In his first speech outside Downing Street, Mr Burnham had promised “a ­circuit breaker for Britain”.

He said his Government would bring forward “the biggest changes in the last 40 years” through “a new political model and a new economic model”.

But he acknowledged that his ten-year plan for delivering that transformation would not be unveiled until later this year.

He instead promised there would be immediate action on the cost-of-living crisis.

He said ­families would get “some breathing space” when he announces his first measures and explains “how we pay for them”.



The former Mayor of Greater Manchester also pledged education reforms, better mental health ­support for young people, more council homes and to end rough sleeping in England.

Ms Mahmood retained the Home Office after narrowly missing out on the Treasury.

Sources close to Ms Mahmood insisted she made clear in the reshuffle process that she wanted to remain in the Home Secretary role.

They said she would now focus on delivering the Government’s pledge to make Britain’s streets safer and create a fairer immigration system.

Yet the scale of the bloodbath left little doubt Mr Burnham wanted a clean break from the Starmer era.



Ms Reeves insisted it had been “the privilege of my life” to serve as Chancellor.

It is understood she was offered a significant job but decided to turn it down.

Former Deputy Prime Minister Mr Lammy said he would have been “proud” to continue serving in Cabinet, but accepted that “a new Prime Minister is entitled to build his own team” and pledged to support the Government from the backbenches.

But former Housing Secretary Steve Reed used his resignation letter to deliver a pointed message to Mr Burnham over his coup.

He wrote: “I hope those who did not show loyalty to Keir will now show it to you.”



Mr Reed also urged him not to overlook southern voters, warning Labour must govern for the whole country if it is to earn a second term in office.

Mr Burnham had been joined by his family for his arrival.

His wife, Dutch-born Marie-France van Heel, was with him outside No10, and he also hugged his mum Eileen.

OUT

MINISTERS bid farewell to Sir Keir Starmer outside Downing Street yesterday. With many losing their jobs, too.

RECOMMENDED STORIES





IN

PRIME Minister Andy Burnham welcomes his new Chancellor of the Exchequer, former Defence ­Secretary John ­Healey, inside No10 — the first appointment of the re­shuffled ­Cabinet.

News.title: ‘Pure evil’ boy, 16, stabbed accountant, 26, to death with machete in ambush after he ‘pestered’ girl for sex
News.content:
A “PURE evil” boy stabbed an accountant to death with a machete after luring him for sex with a 16-year-old girl.

Emmanuel Avogo, then 16, hatched a plan with a girl to “lure” Adam Khan, 26, to a meeting in Luton.



When Khan arrived at Humberstone Road, Avogo chased after him and pulled out a machete before stabbing him.

After being convicted at a murder trial, the boy, now 17, has been handed a life sentence.



Harrow Crown Court heard that Khan had been “pestering” the girl for sex and agreed to provide her with some cannabis.

The girl, who could not be named, planned an attack with Avogo, but she did not know he would be armed with the machete.



CCTV footage of the incident from August 31, 2025, shows Khan approaching a car and talking to the girl through the window.

Suddenly Avogo confronts Khan and pulls out a machete from his trousers.



The accountant retreats into his car and drives away for a short distance with the boy chasing after him.

He stops his vehicle to take a tyre wrench from the boot to face Avogo with.

Khan was stabbed five times – in the face, stomach and arm – in the fight that followed, and died later that evening in hospital.

The judge said: “By August 31 he had offered to get you some cannabis for some form of sexual favour, and most people would agree this was very wrong.

“It would have served him right if you two had taken the drugs and run off, but he had done nothing to deserve the terrible violence done to him that day.”



Khan’s sister dubbed the killers “pure evil” and told them to “rot in hell” as the court heard how the victim had been destined for a successful career as an accountant when he was killed.

On Monday, Avogo was sentenced to life with a minimum term of 20 years.

The girl was sentenced to a two-year detention and training order after she was found guilty at trial of manslaughter.

The court also heard that Avogo regularly carried a knife and had a past involving knives and violence.

The teen had been spared jail, four months before confronting Khan, after stabbing a man with a 67cm-long machete during the robbery of an e-bike.



In 2023, he attempted to push another boy into the road and punching him in the face and also attacked two fellow school pupils.

Avogo also assaulted a police officer in January 2024, and he was caught with a lock knife in August that year, when aged 15.

The judge added: “The seriousness of the offence of which he was convicted and the widespread publicity and concern surrounding young people and knife crime militate in favour of allowing this case to be examined by the press and discussed by the public.”

He stripped Avogo of his anonymity after the Press Association applied to be able to name him as a deterrent against knife crime.

Khan’s mother, who was not named, told the court that her son had started working at 15 after the death of his father to support his family, and she called him “bright, strong, resilient and caring”.



She said of the teenage killers: “I hope they meet a fate far worse than what they inflicted on my son.”

Khan’s sister said that her brother was murdered a day before he was due to take his final accountancy qualification exam, having got himself a job within a top financial firm.

“He had so much to look forward to, but that was brutally snatched from him,” she said.

She said the teenage killers have “pure evil inside of them”, and said: “My brother’s death will hover over our heads and leave a hole in our hearts for the rest of our lives.”

She added: “I pray the harshest of justice is served to the inhumane people who committed this crime.



“May they rot in hell.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Avogo blamed the PTSD he got after being hit in the head with a hammer and having surgery in 2023 as contributing to his confrontation with Khan.

Mr Justice Bennathan noted that the boy continues to plead his innocence over Khan’s death, insisting he had not intended to cause him serious harm.

News.title: Man goes missing at popular lake as urgent search launched just 11 days after another body was pulled from water
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FIND HIM Man goes missing at popular lake as urgent search launched just 11 days after another body was pulled from water

POLICE have launched a search after a man has gone missing at a popular UK lake.

Emergency services were called to Llyn Geirionydd lake in Wales at around 7.10pm on Sunday.



Police helicopters and divers have reportedly been seen scouring the area to find the man.

One witness said that there was a “significant emergency response” as search teams spent the night looking for the missing person.



Llyn Geirionydd is a 45-acre lake nestled on the lower slopes of the Carneddau mountains in Snowdonia.

North Wales Police said that the man’s family has been notified as it continues in its search.

It has told the public to avoid the area as emergency services continue with their work.

The body of a 21-year-old man had recently been recovered from the lake just 11 days ago.

News.title: ‘Shocked’ new mum gives birth to one of Britain’s biggest babies – with newborn already wearing clothes for 6-month-olds
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TITAN TOT ‘Shocked’ new mum gives birth to one of Britain’s biggest babies – with newborn already wearing clothes for 6-month-olds

A MUM has given birth to one of Britain’s biggest babies.

Jenallie Ross, 33, had a C-section earlier this month for her son, who weighs 14 pounds and 2 ounces.



The baby, still unnamed, was just shy of Britain’s heaviest baby who weighed a staggering 15lb 8 oz.

He is already wearing clothes for a three to six month old baby despite being just days old.



And he is going through two bottles worth of milk with Jenallie expecting him to keep growing at a rapid pace.

Jenallie, 33, said: “I couldn’t believe it. I was crying. The first thing I said was ‘where did this big baby come from – he’s so big!’.

“But my tummy was really big – it was really rough carrying him.

“I had to have extra ultrasounds every two weeks to check his growth. The pounds just kept packing on.

“They couldn’t figure out why he was growing so big.

“They told me I had to have a C-section. I didn’t want surgery. I cried so much.



“I had to have extra ultrasounds every two weeks to check his growth. The pounds just kept packing on. They kept doing tests, maybe it was genetic.

“I was scared. I suffered with my blood sugar levels.”

Janallie is 5’7 and the baby’s dad Victor Okanme, 26, is 6ft.

The baby weighed double the weight of Jenallie’s two other children when they were born.

Jenallie, from Milton Keynes, is believed to have smashed hospital records with the birth.



The biggest baby born in Britain on record is Guy Carr, who weighed 15lbs 8oz at birth in 1992.

Other big babies include George King, who was 15lbs 7oz when he was born in 2013.

And Alpha Stone Mitchell was 14lbs 15oz when he was born in 2021.

News.title: UK weather maps show 37C August scorcher with 4-day heatwave - 6 areas above 30C
News.content:
UK weather maps show 37C August scorcher with 4-day heatwave - 6 areas above 30C

Weather maps show another spat of extreme heat will hit the UK next month as areas will see temperatures in the high 30s as the Met Office say August is forecast to be 'very warm'

View 4 Images (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

Brits can expect another wave of extreme weather as heatwave conditions are expected to return at the beginning of next month.

‌



NetWeather weather maps have turned bright red illustrating the high temperatures the UK will experience as the Met Office say conditions could turn “very warm again by the start of August”.

‌



Temperatures will climb at the end of July with much of the nation to bake in extreme heat on Friday, July 31.

‌



View 4 Images The weather is forecast to be the warmest on July 31 (Image: NetWeather)

On this day, areas in the south are expected to see the hottest temperatures with London reaching 32C.

However, the hottest counties are forecast to be Sussex and Gloucestershire at 36C and 37C.

‌



It is likely that if temperatures do reach these levels further heat warnings will be issued, and disruption could be felt across the UK.

All regions above 30C:

South West England

South East England

Greater London

East of England

East Midlands

West Midlands

‌



The heatwave will then continue over the coming days, although temperatures will slightly decrease.

A heatwave is a prolonged period of excessively hot and humid weather, lasting for three or more days typically.

View 4 Images Temperatures will hit sit in the thirties as the hot spell continues (Image: NetWeather)

‌



It is defined relative to the normal climate of a specific location, meaning a temperature that is standard in one region can be considered a heatwave in another.

On Saturday, August 1, temperatures will still sit in the thirties, with London warming up to 33C, according to the weather maps.

Suffolk and Norfolk are also likely to see highs of 34C. The Midlands is also forecast to welcome warms of 31C and 32C.

‌



However, in the South West temperatures will drop dramatically to 27C, still feeling warm for many Brits.

These conditions will slightly change as much of the nation will ease into the twenties on Sunday, August 2. However, in the South East there will still be highs of 31C.

View 4 Images NetWeather map for August 3 (Image: NetWeather)

Article continues below

Starting the next week on Monday, August 3 many areas will remain at similar temperatures with Essex expecting to reach 30C. In the Midlands, many areas are forecast to experience 28C and 29C.

The Met Office forecast for August 2 to August 16 states: “Temperatures will very likely remain above normal, with potential for further hot spells, particularly in the south.”

However alongside these warm conditions there is also chances of stormy weather. It adds: “Although most areas may see dry weather for much of the period, occasional summertime thunderstorms are possible on some days given the right ingredients.”

News.title: Andy Burnham live: New PM to host first cabinet meeting this morning after Donald Trump phone call
News.content:
New Prime Minister, Andy Burnham, has already made a number of sweeping changes to the Cabinet and later this morning he is set to host his first cabinet meeting

Andy Burnham live: New PM to host first cabinet meeting this morning after Donald Trump phone call

Andy Burnham made his first Cabinet appointments yesterday — bringing back Angela Rayner to the fold.

Talking yesterday without a lectern or notes, in a huge move away from tradition, Mr Burnham, 56, spoke for 10 minutes and used the opportunity to outline his vision for the UK. In his first speech as PM, Burnham said an announcement about tackling the cost of living would be made today.

He said he could "do something to give people some breathing space now" and was looking at measures "that could make a difference this year". And confirmed he was "finalising the details" and that some of the measures - including "how we pay for them" - would be set out today.

The new Prime Minister will begin his first full day as prime minister with a cabinet meeting this morning. His team includes John Healey as chancellor, Shabana Mahmood as home secretary, and Ed Miliband as foreign secretary.

News.title: Furniture brand relaunches after plunging into liquidation and closing 36 stores
News.content:
Furniture brand relaunches after plunging into liquidation and closing 36 stores

A popular furniture brand is set to return after it was bought out by a Chinese e-commerce group, giving stores the green light to open up shop once again on the High Street

View 2 Images A woman shopping for wooden furniture (file image) (Image: Carlina Teteris via Getty Images)

A furniture retailer that collapsed earlier this year is set to make a comeback after being rescued from liquidation. European furniture brand Alinea will return after MH France, the French subsidiary of Chinese e-commerce group Aosom, acquired the French retailer's brand and operating rights. The takeover was approved by courts in France on July 9, 2026, before being announced by MH France chief executive Emmanuel Benichou on July 11. Benichou confirmed the acquisition in a post on LinkedIn. He wrote: "Today, I am pleased to announce that the MH France/Aosom.fr group has just acquired the Alinea brand and its operating rights. "Some brands go beyond just their commercial activities; they are part of the landscape and Alinea is one of those brands. Since its creation in 1988 in Avignon, the brand has left its mark on several generations of French people, and the world of furniture and decoration.... Today marks the beginning of a new chapter."

‌



View 2 Images The furniture business is set for a comeback [generic image] (Image: Getty Images)

‌



He added that, as part of the relaunch, Alinea's online store will shortly go live once more, as well as a franchise-based retail network to follow. MH France said it plans to preserve Alinea's identity while combining French and European-inspired collections with imported products. More details about the retailer's long-term strategy are expected in the coming weeks.

‌



The liquidation salvation comes following years of difficulties for the brand prior to Alinea's ultimate demise in March. Placed under court-ordered administration at the end of 2025, the business was later formally liquidated on March 31, 2026. This resulted in the closure of all of its 36 stores and the dismissal of nearly 1,200 staff following the rejection of the only comprehensive takeover bid on offer for the furniture brand. The retailer's website had already stopped accepting orders on February 26, which saw opportunistic scammers launch a number of fake clearance websites impersonating the brand. But now, like a Phoenix rising from the ashes, it seems that Alinea is officially back in business. In his online statement, Benichou emphasised that the Alinea takeover represents "both a responsibility and a tremendous opportunity", and for customers to essentially watch this space in the coming weeks as the brand makes major steps to return to operating capacity. He also reminded fans of the furniture brand to remain vigilant while the brand reboots, with the CEO expressing concerns that scammers may again try to schmooze eager customers out of their hard-earned euros with further fake online stores and websites.

Article continues below

MH France currently retails through a number of e-commerce marketplaces and sells products under a slew of brand names.

News.title: Andy Burnham's first day as PM: From new Cabinet to Donald Trump phone call
News.content:
Andy Burnham's first day as PM: From new Cabinet to Donald Trump phone call

Andy Burnham has been officially appointed as the new Prime Minister of the UK and has wasted no time in getting to work, with a new Cabinet announced and a bold speech delivered on his first day in office

View 4 Images It was a big day for Andy Burnham yesterday (Image: Dan Kitwood, Getty Images)

Andy Burnham became Britain's seventh Prime Minister in a decade on Monday and wasted no time getting down to business in the top job.

‌



His opening day kicked off with a formal audience with the King at Buckingham Palace before he delivered his maiden address as PM on the steps of No 10. Mr Burnham then acted swiftly to name his new Cabinet.

‌



The Makerfield MP, who made his return to Parliament in June following a stint as Mayor of Greater Manchester, was formally elected Leader of the Labour Party on Friday.

‌



View 4 Images United Kingdom. Prime Minister Andy Burnham appoints John Healey as Chancellor of the Exchequer (Image: Simon Dawson / No 10 Downing Street)

Donald Trump shares details of first call with new Prime Minister Andy Burnham READ MORE :

Five die in river tragedy after trying to rescue drowning swimmer in Ohio River READ MORE :

The official transition took place after Sir Keir Starmer submitted his resignation, with the King inviting Mr Burnham to form a government.

"I now pass the baton to Andy Burnham. I wish him every success. He has my full support," Sir Keir Starmer said in his resignation address.

‌



In his inaugural speech outside Downing Street, Mr Burnham pledged to provide early "breathing space" for families grappling with the cost of living crisis, committed to ending rough sleeping and outlined his vision to "reindustrialise Britain".

The new PM said he would deliver "a new political model and a new economic model" for Britain. It was, he said, a moment for "reflection and new resolution", adding that: "Britain needs to show the world that we can regain our stability once again".

He continued: "I know people at home are fed up with politics. I hear you and I want to be honest with you – we have not been good enough, and we need to be better. We will be.

‌



"We will make this moment a circuit breaker for Britain, bringing forward the biggest changes in the last 40 years – a new political model and a new economic model."

Sir John Healey emerged as Mr Burnham's most significant appointment, assuming the role of Chancellor of the Exchequer.

In a statement posted on X, he said: "It is the greatest privilege to be appointed Chancellor of the Exchequer by the Prime Minister. Together, we will build a new economy, build new hope and advance the working people of this country. Time to get on with the job."

‌



View 4 Images Andy Burnham outside Downing Street (Image: Anadolu via Getty Images)

The reshuffled Cabinet saw former Labour leader Ed Miliband handed the Foreign Secretary brief, while Yvette Cooper was moved to the health portfolio. Bridget Phillipson was removed from her position as education secretary but secured a new role as Minister for Women and Equalities, and former deputy prime minister Angela Rayner was installed as Housing Secretary.

Louise Haigh, a close confidante of Mr Burnham who played a crucial part in securing his path to No 10, has been appointed First Secretary of State and Chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster, handing her a troubleshooting remit across Whitehall.

‌



Former health secretary Wes Streeting, who stepped down from Sir Keir Starmer's government, had been viewed as a possible leadership contender before throwing his weight behind Mr Burnham. He was unveiled as the new Defence Secretary on Monday evening.

A number of senior figures kept their posts, including Transport Secretary Heidi Alexander and Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood. Meanwhile, Labour stalwart Pat McFadden will hold on to his position as Work and Pensions Secretary.

Within an hour of stepping through the doors of No 10, Mr Burnham spoke directly with US President Donald Trump, who subsequently wished him "good luck" in a post on Truth Social.

‌



The American leader went on to say that the new PM "has got a big job ahead of him, but he will be able to do it" and promised that the US "will be there to help".

View 4 Images Andy Burnham meets with his Mother Eileen Burnham. (Image: Martin Dalton/Shutterstock)

Mr Burnham also held talks with a number of other prominent world leaders on Monday, amongst them Ukraine's Volodymyr Zelensky, French President Emmanuel Macron and Nato secretary general Mark Rutte.

Article continues below

EU President Antonio Costa took to X to offer his congratulations to Mr Burnham on his appointment. He said: "In the last two years EU-UK relations gained a new, positive momentum. I look forward to continuing to further deepen our cooperation for the benefit of our citizens and businesses. The United Kingdom and the European Union are stronger together."

News.title: Young mother, 21, dies in horror blaze as baby son faces life 'without his mummy'
News.content:
Young mother, 21, dies in horror blaze as baby son faces life 'without his mummy'

Isabella Nicholls' family said they were ' absolutely shattered by this unimaginable loss', describing their heartbreak as 'beyond words' - police are now investigating the fire

View 3 Images Police are now probing the fire which killed Isabella (Image: Stephanie Weatherall/GoFundMe)

A tiny tot is set to grow up without his mum after she tragically passed away in a fire now being investigated by police.

‌



Isabella Nicholls, just 21-years-old, managed to escape the fire at a home in Buderim, on Australia’s Sunshine Coast. She was taken to Royal Brisbane Women’s Hospital, where she sadly died from the serious burns.

‌



Queensland Police said the blaze took hold at 7:30pm on Sunday (July 19) and officers are now appealing for information as they investigate the cause of the inferno.

‌



Isabella’s death has ‘absolutely shattered’ her family, her loved ones said. Her young son, Elijah, will now have to grow up ‘without his mummy’, they added.

“Isabella was a devoted and loving mother to her beautiful baby boy, Elijah, who will now grow up without his mummy,” her family said in a post on GoFundMe to raise cash for her funeral.

View 3 Images Isabella with her beautiful baby Elijah, who now has to 'grow up without his mummy' (Image: Stephanie Weatherall/GoFundMe)

‌



“Our family is absolutely shattered by this unimaginable loss, and the heartbreak is beyond words.

“Isabella was a vibrant, kind, and beautiful soul with her whole life ahead of her. She had a smile that could light up any room and a contagious laugh that none of us will ever forget.

“She touched the lives of so many people with her warmth, compassion, and beautiful spirit, and her absence has left an irreplaceable void in all of our hearts.”

‌



Images shared with the statement show Isabella, originally from Kallangur in Queensland, playing in a paddling pool with Elijah. Her family also shared a photograph of the duo shortly after the tot was born.

Cops are now probing the fire, asking witnesses to come forward.

A spokesperson for Queensland Police said: “Police are investigating a fatal fire at a unit complex at Buderim overnight, July 19.

‌



“Emergency services were initially called to the King Street address around 7:30pm following reports one of the units in the complex was fully engulfed.

View 3 Images Isabella Nicholls was just 21 years old - her family said she had her whole life ahead of her (Image: Stephanie Weatherall/GoFundMe)

"A 21-year-old Kallangur woman who was inside the unit was able to escape and was initially transported to the Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital with serious burns but has since died from her injuries.

‌



“Residents of neighbouring units were also evacuated.

“The cause of the fire remains unknown, and investigations are ongoing. Anyone who may have relevant information or CCTV/dashcam footage to come forward.”

Another woman, 32, was reportedly injured in the blaze, but has survived her wounds.

‌



If you have information for police, contact Policelink by providing information using the online suspicious activity form 24hrs per day at www.police.qld.gov.au/reporting .

Quote this reference number: QP2601400544

Report crime information anonymously via Crime Stoppers . Call 1800 333 000 or report online at www.crimestoppersqld.com.au .

News.title: Tragedy as boy, 3, dies after falling into pond in Merseyside as police investigate
News.content:
Tragedy as boy, 3, dies after falling into pond in Merseyside as police investigate

Emergency services were called to an address in Crosby to reports that a boy had fallen into a pond. Sadly, despite best efforts the three-year-old could not be saved

View 2 Images Brownmoor Lane, Crosby (Image: Liverpool ECHO)

A three-year-old boy has tragically died after falling into a pond on Saturday night.

‌



Emergency services were called to an address on Brownmoor Lane in Crosby after receiving reports that a young boy had fallen into a pond.

‌



Both Merseyside Police and North West Ambulance Service rushed to the scene of the incident before assessing the boy, who has not been identified, and transporting him to a nearby hospital. Despite best efforts from paramedics and hospital staff the boy was pronounced dead later that day.

‌



View 2 Images The boy was rushed to hospital

His death is not believed to be suspicious, according to police.

‌



Officers are continuing to support the family of the young boy and enquiries remain ongoing to establish the full circumstances of what happened.

A spokesperson for Merseyside Police said: "We can confirm that emergency services were called to an address on Brownmoor Lane in Crosby on Saturday evening (July 18) following a report a three-year-old boy had fallen into a pond.

"The North West Ambulance Service and police attended and the child was taken by ambulance to hospital for treatment where he was sadly pronounced deceased. Our officers continue to support the family and enquiries are ongoing to establish the full circumstances of what happened."

Article continues below

No further details surrounding the incident or the boy's identity have been released by authorities at this stage.

News.title: Latest FCDO Dubai travel advice for UK holidaymakers after Iran strikes
News.content:
Latest FCDO Dubai travel advice for UK holidaymakers after Iran strikes

The US and Israel carried out strikes on Iran in February and the country retaliated by closing the Strait of Hormuz waterway and striking sites across the Middle East - including Dubai

View 3 Images Jumeira Open Beach with tourists and skyline of skyscrapers in Dubai United Arab Emirates (Image: Getty Images/arabianEye)

Brits travelling to Dubai over the summer may be feeling uncertainty since the latest escalation in the in the Middle East war between the US and Iran.

‌



Monday marked the nineth consecutive day of US strikes on dozens of Iranian sites after tensions flared when both sides abandoned a short-term ceasefire agreement earlier this month.

‌



The US and Iran have been in conflict since February when the US and Israel carried out joint strikes on several key Iranian targets. Iran retaliated by closing the Strait of Hormuz waterway and striking sites across the Middle East - including Dubai.

‌



View 3 Images Three boys play in the shallow waters of the Strait of Hormuz, as a plume of smoke rises from an explosion in the background, off Bandar Abbas, Iran, Monday, July 13, 2026 (Image: AP Photo/Razieh Poudat)

Despite the escalations, the UK's Foreign Office (FCDO) has not changed its advice for travel to the United Arab Emirates since it removed its "all but essential travel" advisory published on June 18.

Just one day earlier, the US and Iran signed a Memorandum of Understanding to bring the war to a close within 60 days. This appears to have failed. This means that people can travel to the UAE without having their travel insurance invalidated.

‌



What does this mean for Brits travelling to the UAE?

The FCDO no longer advises against all but essential travel to the UAE, but warns that "the situation remains unpredictable and attacks could resume at short notice". The warning stands as of Monday, 20 July.

British nationals should read the FCDO's crisis abroad document, follow advice from local authorities and sign up to FCDO travel advice email alerts.

If conflict resumes, it advises travellers to stay away from areas around security or military facilities, keep departure plans and travel documents up to date and remain indoors if told to take shelter.

‌



View 3 Images US Marines board Iranian-flagged ship in Gulf of Oman on July 16, 2026 (Image: CENTCOM / SWNS)

The FCDO no longer warns against non-essential travel to the UAE, so travel insurance is likely to be valid if booking a trip now. However, your travel insurance is at risk of being invalidated if you travel against advice from FCDO. It is important to check individual policies.

Package holidays are likely to start operating as usual and there are no grounds for travellers to expect a refund if they cancel, nor to claim the money back through travel insurance.

Article continues below

If FCDO advice changes to advising against all travel, you can cancel a package holiday without penalty for a full refund.

News.title: Five die in river tragedy after trying to rescue drowning swimmer in Ohio River
News.content:
Five die in river tragedy after trying to rescue drowning swimmer in Ohio River

Emergency services were called after a terrified young child was seen by motorists running along a major road, police have now confirmed two women and three men died in the river tragedy in Ohio

View 2 Images Rescue crews searching the river in Ohio (Image: WCMH)

Five people have died after attempting to rescue a person who was struggling to swim in a river, police have confirmed.

‌



On Sunday July 19 a group of people had gathered along the Scioto River in the Columbus suburb of Powell in Ohio when one of them went into the river for a swim. “That’s when the tragedy started to occur,” Delaware County Sheriff Jeffrey Balzer said at a news conference. He said others who jumped in to help also began struggling.

‌



Several of them went into the water to help the person who was struggling to swim, authorities said Monday. A motorist called the emergency services after spotting a frightened child with the group who was running along a nearby road to seek help, Balzer said.

‌



View 2 Images A view of the Scioto River near where multiple people died (Image: AP Photo/Jay LaPrete)

Rescue crews searching the water later Sunday found two women who were pronounced dead at a hospital, Balzer said. The bodies of three men were found in the river on Monday, said Tracy Whited, a spokesperson for the Delaware County Sheriff’s Department. Authorities did not say exactly where the victims were found.

‌



The river was running high and fast on Sunday, according to data from a U.S. Geological Survey water gauge at the nearby dam. The data shows the water was flowing at a rate of about 350 cubic feet (10 cubic meters) per second on Sunday — more than a fourfold increase over a three-day span, and more than double the average rate.

The tragedy occurred two days after five people were killed in southern Utah after a flash flood swept through scenic red rock canyons during a hiking excursion.

The Ohio sheriff said the child who ran for help, prompting the 911 call, has been placed in the care of family services along with another child under the age of 10. Authorities were working on notifying relatives of the victims, he said.

Article continues below

Balzer said people who gather near water must be aware of the conditions and take precautions.

“Know your skill level before you get in the water. Are you a confident swimmer?” Balzer said. “Make sure you have other people around in case something goes wrong to notify someone.”

News.title: Burnham pledges to 'bring back hope' as he makes Healey chancellor
News.content:
Andy Burnham pledged to "bring back hope" to Britain, as he began his tenure as prime minister by appointing Labour stalwart John Healey as chancellor.

In his first speech to the nation in Downing Street, Burnham said he wanted to bring forward the "biggest changes in the last 40 years" to British politics.

He outlined his intention to unveil a 10-year "new plan for Britain" later this year, explaining this would lay out a path to where he believes "we all want Britain to be".

Burnham promised to make announcements this week to "give people some breathing space now, some help with the cost of living" and explain how he would pay for them.

Burnham also started making cabinet appointments after removing loyalists of former PM Sir Keir Starmer. Out went Rachel Reeves as chancellor, David Lammy as deputy prime minister and justice secretary, and Steve Reed as communities secretary.

Healey, who quit Sir Keir's government due to a row over defence spending, was in as chancellor.

With Burnham saying he wants to honour the UK's commitments on defence spending, Healey will face the challenge of finding the extra money he believed the last government failed to deliver to keep the UK safe.

Speaking to broadcasters, Healey said the pair will "work in lockstep to meet the fiscal rules with a buffer against uncertainty" and on how they will "make life more affordable for working people right across the UK".

Ed Miliband moves from energy secretary to foreign secretary, replacing Yvette Cooper who is now the health secretary.

Miliband told the BBC it was the "honour of my lifetime" to become foreign secretary, a role his brother David held between 2007 and 2010.

Shabana Mahmood remains as home secretary and Louise Haigh takes on the role of Burnham's fixer across government, serving as first secretary of state, chancellor of the Duchy of Lancaster and minister for the Cabinet Office.

Angela Rayner returned to a cabinet job as housing secretary, a role she previously held in Sir Keir's government. She stood down in September 2025 after admitting she underpaid stamp duty on her Â£800,000 flat in Hove.

Wes Streeting, the former health secretary who at one stage was seen as a possible leadership challenger, is the new defence secretary.

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch welcomed Burnham to his new role but said he has not "set out a clear plan for government".

She said "Britain needs a leader who can take difficult decisions, not a people pleaser" and criticised him for "promising to undo Margaret Thatcher's policies".

News.title: Who's in Andy Burnham's cabinet?
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has started building his new cabinet after taking office following the resignation of Sir Keir Starmer.

Tap or click on a cabinet member in our interactive guide below to learn more about them and their role in government. The guide will be updated as new appointments are made.

News.title: Man, 28, charged with murder of Ann Widdecombe
News.content:
A 28-year-old man has been charged with the murder of Ann Widdecombe, police and prosecutors have said.

Joshua Kerry, from Rotherham in South Yorkshire, is set to appear at Westminster Magistrates' Court on Tuesday.

Counter Terrorism Policing said "determining the motivation, including any possible political motivation" remains "an active avenue" of investigation.

Kerry was initially arrested on suspicion of murder on 11 July, before being additionally arrested on 13 July on suspicion of the commission, preparation or instigation of acts of terrorism.

Widdecombe, 78, a former Conservative minister and Reform UK spokeswoman, was found dead on Thursday 9 July at her home in Haytor, Devon, having sustained serious injuries.

In a statement read outside New Scotland Yard, Laurence Taylor, head of UK Counter Terrorism Policing said: "I want to make it very clear that our investigation into [Kerry], determining his motivations and any wider activity he may have been involved in is continuing."

"As with all murder investigations, understanding the 'why' is a key part of our enquiries," he said, adding that it was "a particularly intensive and complex investigation".

Taylor said it remained the case that investigators were not looking for anyone else in connection with the incident.

He added that counter terrorism teams have gathered "a huge amount of information" over the last week, leading to more than 800 lines of enquiry.

The investigation, which remains ongoing, has been led by Counter Terrorism Policing South East, supported by Devon and Cornwall Police.

Frank Ferguson, of the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS)'s special crime and counter terrorism division, said: "Our prosecutors have worked closely with the police to establish that there is sufficient evidence to bring this case to court, and we will continue working with them as their investigation progresses."

"We remind all concerned that proceedings against the defendant are active and he has the right to a fair trial," Ferguson said.

"It is vital that there should be no reporting, commentary or sharing of information which could in anyway prejudice these proceedings."

News.title: At least 27 dead and 83 missing after passenger ferry capsizes off Guyana
News.content:
At least 27 people have drowned after a passenger ferry capsized off the coast of Guyana on Saturday night local time.

Sixty-nine people aboard the MV Barima had been rescued, Prime Minister Mark Phillips told reporters on Monday, adding 83 more remained missing.

Divers continue to search the site where the vessel capsized and people who believe their loved ones may have been on board the stricken vessel have been asked to contact the authorities.

"Our focus again is on finding people," said Phillips. "We still have hope."

An investigation into the tragedy had been launched, he said earlier.

"Let me be absolutely clear: where negligence, misconduct or criminal wrongdoing is established, those responsible will face the full force of the law," he said.

Guyana's Public Works Minister, Juan Edghill, expressed his anger at a news conference on Sunday, accusing those who operated the ferry of trying to "cheat the system".

The official registry had listed 133 as being on board the ferry, but Phillips said on Monday he was now "confident" there were 179 people.

Edghill also said the ferry's captain and at least one crew member had tested positive for cannabis.

"We have zero tolerance for members of the crew drinking or smoking while at work. And for us to have positive tests from the captain... this is serious," the minister said.

He added the captain and several of his crew had been taken into police custody.

News.title: Watch: Spain World Cup champions receive royal welcome in Madrid
News.content:
The Spain World Cup champions met with King Felipe VI, Queen Letizia and their daughters, Princess Leonor and Princess SofÃ­a after arriving back home in Madrid. The royal family payed tribute to the team's talent, determination and historic achievement.

The team capped off the celebrations with a raucous open-top bus victory parade through Madrid, where nearly two million fans lined the streets to welcome the world champions home.

This comes after Spain beat Argentina 1-0 in the final of the World Cup in New Jersey on Sunday night.

News.title: Watch: 'My flat was turned into a brothel,' landlord tells BBC Panorama
News.content:
A BBC Panorama investigation has uncovered how organised crime gangs are exploiting the UK's private rental market - targeting properties to take over and use for their operations.

Among those featured in a new documentary is landlord and property developer Craig Shepheard, who discovered his flat was being used by a prostitution ring, run by a network in Brazil.

BBC Panorama reporter Hazel Martin also found that criminals are using fake IDs to get rental agreements.

News.title: Russian warship carried out firing exercise off Plymouth coast
News.content:
A Russian warship, shadowed by a Royal Navy vessel, carried out a live-fire artillery exercise just 40 nautical miles south of Plymouth on Monday.

The Royal Navy monitored the exercise and is continuing to "track the vessel's activity closely", a Ministry of Defence (MoD) spokesperson said.

The Russian frigate, Neustrashimy, was also being monitored by a French military aircraft which made radio contact with the warship asking it to clarify its intentions, the BBC has been told.

Prior to opening fire, the BBC was also told that the Russian warship informed the Royal Navy Offshore Patrol Vessel, HMS Tyne, of its intention to conduct gunnery activity.

The Russian warship requested that that HMS Tyne reposition to a safer distance, which it did. The Russian live-fire exercise took place in international waters and lasted for 30 minutes.

The incident will be a reminder for the new prime minister of increased Russian naval activity near UK waters in recent months. UK defence sources would not comment on whether the incident might have been timed to coincide with the start of Andy Burnham's premiership.

Last month, Royal Marine Commandos boarded a Russian "shadow fleet" oil tanker in the English Channel in a six-hour operation which was the first of its kind by UK armed forces.

Also in June, a British couple in international waters in the English Channel came across a Russian warship - Admiral Grigorovich - 23 miles (37km) off the Isle of Wight.

The frigate fired warning shots as Jane and Alan Kelvey sailed their yacht on what Russia's defence ministry said had been a "dangerous approach". However, the couple said they were "not on a collision course".

Russian warships regularly pass through international waters in the Channel, which are separate from UK and French territorial waters.

Additional reporting by Ella Kipling

News.title: Is UK facing drought for second summer in a row?
News.content:
Summer so far has been exceptionally hot and dry across much of the UK, with three widespread heatwaves and the longest run of dry days in central England since 1995.

England, Wales and eastern Scotland have been the driest areas over recent weeks, and this follows a very dry spring in similar regions.

Very little rainfall is forecast through this week for most places, with only a few light showers possible, mainly close to coasts.

As we head through the second half of summer, what are the longer range predictions, and are we heading into drought for the second summer in a row?

News.title: Kevin Keegan, Liverpool footballer who managed England and Newcastle United, dies aged 75
News.content:
Former England captain and manager Kevin Keegan has died at the age of 75, seven weeks after he revealed he had been diagnosed with stage four cancer, his family have confirmed.

One of English football's most decorated players, Keegan enjoyed spells at Scunthorpe United, Liverpool, Hamburg, Southampton and Newcastle during an illustrious playing career.

He later went on to manage Newcastle, Fulham, England and Manchester City.

Keegan revealed he had stage four cancer in June, which is the most advanced stage of cancer and means the disease has spread to other parts of the body.

His family initially disclosed he was battling the disease in January, after he had "further evaluation of ongoing abdominal symptoms" in hospital.

A statement on behalf of the Keegan family said he was "surrounded by his wife and daughters in his final moments".

"Kevin, a double Ballon d'Or winner, was a much loved husband, father and grandfather," it continued.

"The family would like to thank Kevin's incredible medical team for all their support. This is a hugely difficult time and they are requesting space and privacy."

Newcastle United paid tribute, describing Keegan as "one of the most iconic, influential and deeply loved figures in our club's history".

The club statement added: "Kevin was more than a legendary footballer and manager. He was the beating heart of Newcastle United for generations of supporters.

"Kevin's impact will not be measured by appearances or results. It will live on in the memories he created with club and country, the dreams he inspired wherever he went, and the generations of supporters around the world who fell in love with football because of him."

Liverpool, for whom Keegan played for between 1971 and 1977, said Keegan's "indomitable spirit and remarkable contribution will be forever etched in our history and his legacy will live on".

Hamburg said football had lost one of its "defining figures" and they would always "cherish" his memory, while Fulham said Keegan "forged a strong connection" with the fans, who would "forever hold wonderful memories" of his short time at the club.

Keegan's first club, Scunthorpe, described him as "one of the best players of his generation", with an "inspirational demeanour" and "brilliant personality".

England and Manchester City both offered their condolences to the Keegan family, with the latter describing him as "one of the most iconic and fondly remembered figures in English football".

The Three Lions will celebrate Keegan's life when they host Spain in a Uefa Nations League match at Wembley on 26 September.

News.title: Ofcom launches investigation into Married at First Sight UK
News.content:
Married at First Sight UK is facing renewed pressure after the broadcast regulator launched an official investigation into the hit Channel 4 reality TV show.

In a statement on Monday, Ofcom said it was investigating "a fairness and privacy complaint" about the prime-time show.

In May, a BBC Panorama investigation revealed rape allegations from two female cast members on the show - allegations the men involved deny.

An Ofcom fairness or privacy complaint can be lodged by individuals who participated in TV or radio programmes. Complaints like these usually relate to claims of being treated unfairly or having unwarranted infringements of privacy on programmes.

It is understood the watchdog is considering a complaint of unjust or unfair treatment from a cast member of Married at First Sight UK.

At least one other cast member previously complained to Ofcom about their treatment on the show, but the watchdog dismissed their complaint as it found the broadcaster had no case to answer.

An Ofcom spokesperson said such complaints are considered "on a case-by-case basis through a detailed and careful assessment process".

News.title: South East Water hosepipe ban to affect 2.4 million people
News.content:
A hosepipe ban has been expanded to cover 2.4 million people across the south of England after record-breaking temperatures.

South East Water's ban now includes parts of Sussex, Surrey, Hampshire and Berkshire - an extra 1.5m customers. A ban in parts of Kent has been in force since 3 July.

Douglas Whitfield, SEW's water supply director, said it was "deeply sorry" and "incredibly grateful to everyone helping us protect water supplies" after exceptionally hot and dry weather.

Eastbourne MP Josh Babarinde said he was "appalled", calling it "the direct result of years of underinvestment in upgrading infrastructure and building resilience".

Under the restrictions, households in the affected area will be banned from using a hosepipe in their homes for tasks including cleaning, filling ponds, or watering plants.

The ban will officially come in from 00:01 BST on Saturday, but SEW has asked its customers to abide by the restrictions immediately.

The UK record for the hottest day in June was broken for a third day in a row last month, with temperatures reaching 37.3C, the Met Office said.

News.title: Sara Sharif killer wants inquest with jury
News.content:
The woman who murdered her stepdaughter Sara Sharif has asked for the inquest into her death to be held in front of a jury.

Beinash Batool and Sara's father Urfan Sharif were jailed for life in 2024 after the 10-year-old was found dead at the family home in Woking.

She had been violently abused in a "campaign of torture" lasting two years.

Bite marks, an iron burn and scalding from hot water were among dozens of injuries found on her body in a post-mortem examination.

On Monday, Batool's lawyer Dr Anton van Dellen said jurors would help determine if Sara was failed by people who were scared of being accused of racism.

"This is just the type of judgement where a diverse local jury would provide a helpful perspective," he added.

A review into the 10-year-old's death found that services in Surrey failed to properly investigate why Sara started wearing a hijab - that covered her bruising - for "fear of causing offence".

Neighbours also said they were worried about "being branded as being racist" if they reported concerns.

News.title: Ryanair profits drop as Iran war puts off passengers and lifts fuel costs
News.content:
Ryanair's profits have fallen sharply as war in the Middle East sent jet fuel prices soaring and customers reluctant to book flights.

The Irish airline's pre-tax profits dropped 34% to â¬593m (Â£503m) between April and June while sales were flat as the company was forced to cut fares to stimulate demand.

Ryanair also said it expects summer fares to be slightly lower than last year due to "consumer hesitancy" around air travel.

The price of fuelling a plane has jumped since the US and Israel launched strikes against Iran in February and while Ryanair said it had "hedged" or struck deals for the most future fuel costs, those not included in these arrangements had more than doubled.

Crude oil prices hit $90 (Â£67) a barrel for the first time in a month on Monday, before falling back slightly, after a weekend of intense exchanges of fire between the US and Iran.

Traffic through the Strait of Hormuz â an essential route for global oil and gas supplies â has ground to a halt.

An interim peace deal last month brought some respite to oil and energy prices, but they spiked again as negotiations broke down and fighting resumed.

The airline warned that its results for the year will be "highly sensitive" to external factors such as conflict escalation in the Middle East and Ukraine as well as the price of unhedged jet fuel.

Fares for for the key summer period between July and September are on track to be "modestly" lower than last year, with many passengers booking closer to departure than normal.

The firm's finance chief, Neil Sorahan, said flights on its popular Mediterranean routes were still full. "People [are] as keen to get away as ever, albeit booking just a little bit later," he said.

Between April and June, Ryanair's revenue ticked up 1% to â¬4.4bn.

While passenger numbers rose 6% to 6.1 million- helped by the Easter holiday in April - fares fell by 6% as the airline reduced fares to entice flyers concerned about the Iran war.

Ryanair's share price fell 5% on Monday.

Russ Mould, investment director at AJ Bell, said Ryanair was in a better position than many of its rivals, but nonetheless "visibility is worse than San Francisco airport when the fog sets in".

"The renewed escalation in hostilities in the Middle East is unhelpful and without a lasting resolution, challenging times for the airline and travel space look set to continue."

News.title: Ofcom unable to take further legal action against suicide forum
News.content:
Ofcom said it is unable to take further legal action against a pro-suicide forum which campaigners say has been linked to over 130 UK deaths.

The regulator said, external the site had blocked access for the "vast majority" of UK users, and it had "no further legal routes available" under the Online Safety Act.

But it accepted people would still be able to access the forum by using a VPN, which hides your location online.

Andy Burrows, chief executive of the Molly Rose Foundation, said the decision to take no further legal action would "result in more lost lives" and that announcing it on the day a new prime minister was named showed "an utter lack of moral courage".

In response, an Ofcom spokesperson said it had made the decision a "matter of days ago" following "months of work to exhaust all possible legal routes".

They said bereaved families were informed of the decision this morning after being contacted last week.

"In that context, we do not consider it appropriate to delay the announcement further to accommodate today's political developments," they said.

Meanwhile, Ofcom enforcement director Suzanne Cater said the regulator had used its powers "to the fullest extent possible".

"We'll continue to monitor the forum closely to check the geoblock remains in place," she said.

The geoblock means people based in the UK are unable to access the site, unless they mask their location through a VPN or similar means.

Ofcom said it was working with the government to explore whether its enforcement powers should be strengthened.

In particular, this concerns its ability to get a website blocking order through the courts, which would legally mandate internet service providers in the UK to block the website.

The regulator says it has reached the limit of what it can legally do under the Online Safety Act because the forum has implemented the geoblock.

The BBC has approached the government for comment.

News.title: 'Scrutiny' needed over baby's death, court hears
News.content:
Preston had been taken to Blackpool Victoria Hospital three times before his death and seen by a "battery of professionals" including medical staff, social workers and welfare officers from various bodies.

Wilson told the hearing an inquest had initially been opened shortly after Preston's death but was then suspended while police investigated, culminating in the trial and conviction of his adoptive parents.

Wilson said he had to consider whether an inquest should continue, given "relevant issues" had already been heard during the eight-week criminal trial.

However, while he said he would not make a final decision on Monday, subject to submissions from lawyers for other public bodies, it was "highly likely" one would take place, probably in the autumn of next year.

He said: "I feel there's sufficient reason to resume. There are acts and omissions of public authorities that need to be scrutinised in a public hearing in which Preston's family can participate.

"It's clearly going to be a wide-ranging inquiry."

The coroner said he was aware there had been calls for a public inquiry, but his role meant that was not a matter for himself to consider, but to proceed on the basis of whether or not to hold an inquest.

The court heard Oldham Safeguarding Children's Partnership, had resumed a review into Preston's death, following its suspension for the criminal trial to take place.

This review was likely only to be completed by January 2027, and the inquest cannot be held before then, the court heard.

Much of the hearing dealt with which people or public bodies should be legally represented at any inquest.

They included Preston's biological mother and grandmother, Sara and Debbie Davey, neither of whom were present for the hearing but were represented by lawyers in court.

Preston was born while his mother was in custody and a place in a mother and baby unit in prison was refused, the court heard.

Instead, he was taken from her by a court order from Oldham Council and placed with temporary adoptive parents before being adopted by Varley and McGowan.

News.title: Fire crews to remain at Arthur's Seat for days after blaze
News.content:
Firefighters are expected to remain at Arthur's Seat in Edinburgh "for a couple of days" following a large blaze on Sunday evening.

Small plumes of smoke could still be seen on Monday morning along Salisbury Crags and large swathes of vegetation below the cliff face had been burned black.

Six fire engines were sent to tackle the the grassfire on the slope between the Scottish Parliament and St Leonard's, with crews working overnight to douse the flames and dampen hotspots.

The Scottish Fire and Rescue Service (SFRS) said there were "no reported casualties" but Police Scotland said Queen's Drive, the road that encircles the Holyrood Park hills, remained closed to all vehicles.

It is the second fire in the last three months at the landmark, an ancient extinct volcano that offers panoramic views of the Scottish capital.

A Very High risk of wildfire warning for the central Highlands, southern and eastern Scotland has been extended to Friday as warm weather is forecast to continue.

The warning was extended by the SFRS, in conjunction with the Scottish Wildfire Forum (SWF).

Robotaxi firm Zoox has issued a software recall after one of its vehicles drove into smoke near a fire scene in Las Vegas.

About 100 vehicles from the Amazon-owned company were potentially affected by the software issue, which was discovered after the June 20 incident, according to a National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recall report submitted Thursday.

On that day, an unoccupied Zoox vehicle encountered heavy smoke, obscuring a fire scene that was not blocked off with traffic cones. The report didn’t specify where the incident took place, but a person with knowledge of the matter told The Independent that it happened in Vegas.

After entering the fire scene, the robotaxi braked hard as it attempted to steer away. Guided by a remote operator, the vehicle reversed, and then first responders placed cones to block off two of the three lanes of traffic.

open image in gallery Robotaxi firm Zoox has issued a software recall after one of its vehicles drove into smoke near a fire scene in Las Vegas ( AFP via Getty Images )

Within days of the incident, Zoox notified federal regulators and launched its own investigation into the matter. The probe found that the June 20 incident was the “only event of this kind that Zoox has experienced” and no injuries were discovered.

Federal regulators said Zoox developed a software update that “enhances existing capability of detecting and responding to heavy smoke including active EV [emergency vehicle] scenes.”

A spokesperson for the California-based company told The Independent, “Safety is foundational at Zoox. We value our work with first responders, city officials, and regulators to continue to ensure we’re driving safely in the communities we serve."

open image in gallery About 100 vehicles from the Amazon-owned company Zoox were potentially affected by a software issue ( Getty Images )

This is not the first time Zoox vehicles have been subject to a recall.

A National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recall report from December noted that Zoox had to update its robotaxi software after discovering its vehicles crossed lanes “unnecessarily” at or near intersections in certain circumstances.

Amazon acquired Zoox in 2020, about six years after the company was formed.

Zoox officially launched its robotaxi service on and around the Las Vegas Strip in September. The company started offering rides to the public in San Francisco in November.

A Morgan Wallen fan has claimed that he and his family were urinated on during a concert in Baltimore, and police are now investigating.

The incident occurred while the 33-year-old country superstar was performing at the city’s M&T Bank Stadium on Saturday, July 18.

The fan, whose name is Troy Grevelding, alleges that he was watching the performance along with his wife, brother and 8-year-old niece when an unidentified concertgoer behind them exposed himself before urinating freely, splashing the family.

Grevelding says the man was ejected by concert security, but that Maryland State Police said they couldn’t arrest the man as they hadn’t witnessed the incident.

In a video circulating on social media, Grevelding can be heard in conversation with officers.

A Morgan Wallen fan has alleged a fellow concertgoer peed on his family ( Getty )

“There’s nothing we can do about a guy physically pulling out his dick and pissing on me right now? In front of an 8-year-old girl?” asks Grevelding.

The Maryland officer responds to say: “We cannot take him into custody. We’re going to give you his information, and you can be referred to the commissioner.”

Grevelding then addresses the camera and says: “I’m going to make it known that I had a gentleman whip his dick out at a Morgan Wallen concert, piss on me, my brother and my niece, and the Maryland State Police can do nothing about it. Not a thing.”

In a statement to TMZ, MDTA Police said that they are "aware of this incident and the video that is on social media. There is an active and open criminal investigation into this matter."

Wallen’s performance in Baltimore was part of his ongoing “Still The Problem” tour, which continues in Ann Arbor, Michigan this week before concluding in Philadelphia at the start of August.

Last month, Wallen cancelled one of his tour dates in Pittsburgh due to bad weather. Backlash immediately ensued as fans complained that canceling the show was unnecessary because the predicted thunderstorms were not near the concert venue, and the bad weather ended hours before the show was scheduled to begin.

The country star claimed that after speaking with “local officials,” he had “no choice” but to call off the show.

However, Pittsburgh Mayor Corey O’Connor later denied that any conversation with city officials took place and said that Wallen had “no contact” before making his decision.

An earlier date in the tour also sparked controversy after video circulated of Wallen flipping his piano on stage.
