World.title: Sask. Roughrider in fatal crash was driving on wrong side of divided highway: RCMP
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

Saskatchewan Roughriders linebacker Jayden Dalke was driving the wrong way on the highway with alcohol and cannabis in his vehicle before the crash that killed him and another driver, RCMP say.

Saskatchewan RCMP sent a news release Monday morning saying officers responded to a crash Saturday night at 9 p.m. CST.

RCMP say investigation found Dalke had been driving a silver SUV northbound in the southbound lane on Highway 11 between Regina and Lumsden. The entire stretch of Highway 11 between Regina and Lumsden is divided, with two lanes in each direction.

Dalke's SUV collided with a black SUV about nine kilometres southeast of Lumsden.

Both drivers died in the crash and both were the only ones in their vehicles.

Bhishma Rajyaguru, 22, of Regina was identified as the driver of the other vehicle.

Sask. RCMP say 22-year-old Bhishma Rajyaguru died in a fatal crash near Lumsden, Sask., on Saturday night. (Submitted by Dakshesh Raval)

The families of Rajyaguru and Dalke, 30, who was from Leduc, Alta., have both been notified.

RCMP spokeswoman Mandy Maier told reporters at a news conference Monday that no more details were available about the alcohol and cannabis found in Dalke's vehicle.

She asked people to be kind in their online comments out of respect for the grieving families.

"There's a lot of people who are hurting right now," Maier said. "There are two people deceased. This is extremely tragic. Additionally, they were very young and they were just living their life, right, on Saturday night."

RCMP did not receive any reports about a vehicle travelling the wrong way on the highway prior to the crash, Maier said. However, she revealed that RCMP received a report at 8:27 p.m. CST about a silver SUV having left a gas station in Lumsden without paying for fuel, and that further investigation found it was the same SUV that was in the crash.

She also acknowledged the RCMP could have released information about the crash earlier. The information released was determined after "extensive consultation" to ensure the details were accurate.

"News travels fast on social media," Maier said. "And we realize that the RCMP is an official source of information."

Flowers have been placed near Highway 11 southeast of Lumsden where the crash that killed Saskatchewan Roughriders linebacker Jayden Dalke, 30, of Leduc, Alta., and Bhishma Rajyaguru, 22, of Regina happened Saturday night. This photo was taken on Monday, July 20, 2026. (Kirk Fraser/CBC)

Maier said she could not provide an estimate of when autopsies and toxicology tests will be completed. She said collision reconstruction investigations can take months.

RCMP do not usually reveal the names of those killed in crashes, Maier said, pointing to the public interest in this case.

She added that because both occupants were killed and there will be no court proceedings, some questions about the incident may remain unanswered.

"We may never know, right, we have no one surviving from this collision," Maier said. "But the reality is we may never know the answers to many of the questions we all have."

Rajyaguru​'s friends have started an online fundraiser in the wake of his death.

"His parents in India are currently facing the nightmare that no parent should ever have to endure: the loss of their chil​d," the page for the campaign says.

​"We, his friends here in Canada, are coming together to ensure that Bhishma is transported back home so his family can hold him one last time and lay him to rest​."

The fundraiser organizers described Rajyaguru as a "beautiful soul, a best friend, and a beacon of light," and called the crash as "a senseless tragedy that has shattered the hearts of everyone who knew him.​"

Police have identified 22-year-old Bhishma Rajyaguru as a victim of the fatal crash near Lumsden, Sask., on Saturday night. In an online fundraiser, his friends say they have 'lost a beautiful soul, a best friend, and a beacon of light.' (Submitted by Dakshesh Raval)

RCMP say cannabis and alcohol were found in Dalke's vehicle, and that autopsies and toxicology reports will be conducted.

The Riders drafted Dalke in the sixth round of the CFL draft in 2022. Information on the Roughriders website says Dalke was returning to Regina after spending the team's bye week in Leduc.

Roughriders general manager Jeremy O'Day spoke to media about Dalke on Monday morning, before RCMP had released details of the crash.

"In football he was tough and reliable, accountable. Never wanted to let anyone down. He was someone that always wanted to do good for his teammates."

O'Day offered condolences on behalf of the CFL.

"To Jayden's family, his friends, anyone that that has come in touch with Jayden. You know, we're deeply saddened by this tragic event," said O'Day.

The Lumsden RCMP detachment is investigating the crash with the help of an RCMP collision reconstructionist.

World.title: Trump tells Carney to take action on wildfire smoke during World Cup chat
World.content: The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results. U.S. President Donald Trump personally told Prime Minister Mark Carney to stop poisoning American air and take action to put out wildfires burning across the country. Trump said he raised the issue of wildfire management with Carney when the two leaders appeared together to watch the World Cup Final between Argentina and Spain in East Rutherford, N.J., on Sunday. "I told him, I mean, 'You got to stop these fires from coming in and, you know, poisoning our air. Our air has been poisoned,'" Trump said at Joint Base Andrews after the game. The U.S. president said he has a "good relationship" with Carney before reiterating his threat to impose financial penalties on his northern neighbour for the wildfires' impact on U.S. air quality. "If we can help them, we'll help them. But maybe they should pay some damages or something, or we should do some tariffs. But it was terrible," Trump said. "I mean you had businesses closing in particular Michigan." WATCH | Carney explains what he told Trump about Canada's wildfires: Carney says he told Trump that Canada is 'managing' the wildfires | Duration 1:52 Prime Minister Mark Carney says he 'made very clear' the scale of investments and resources Canada is putting on the front lines to fight wildfires across the country when he spoke to U.S. President Donald Trump over the weekend. On Sunday, Trump said he might 'do some tariffs' on Canada if wildfire smoke drifting into U.S. states didn't abate. Carney said Monday he had "made very clear" to Trump that Canada was doing its utmost to control the wildfires. During recent conversations with the U.S. president, Carney told CBC News that he had conveyed the size of the problem, including "the scale of the forest that Canada is blessed with — eight times the size of Texas — [and] the fact that we have effectively drought conditions that have extended from the equivalent of Texas all the way to Minnesota, to put it in American terms." Carney also said he had highlighted Canada's investments in firefighting: "$12 billion in recent years, but fundamentally more than 5,000 brave women and men — firefighters — on those front lines." The prime minister also said he underscored Canada's contributions during American disasters. Managing the situation was "a complex issue," Carney acknowledged. "It's one we're managing and we'll continue to do that." Last week, cities in Michigan shut down beaches, splash pads, the Red Oaks water park and even indoor pools because of the toxic smoke that blanketed Michigan and other northern U.S. states. The Detroit Free Press reported that dozens of workers at Ford's Michigan assembly plant were taken to hospital after inhaling wildfire smoke inside non-air-conditioned plants. Trump's threats over wildfires Trump first threatened to make Canada pay for the cost of U.S. air quality in a Friday social media post when he joined some Republican House representatives' broad criticism of Canada's forest management practices calling them "wilful negligence." "We are holding Canada responsible for the fact that they are not properly maintaining their Forests, and brush therein, and the United States is being unnecessarily invaded by filthy, polluted and unhealthy air," the president wrote in a social media post on Friday. "This is Willful Negligence, and becoming a yearly occurrence, costing the United States Billions of Dollars, which cost of this pollution must of necessity be added to the TARIFFS Canada is currently paying." This morning, I met with federal workers in Ottawa who are supporting the wildfire response efforts in Northwestern Ontario and across the country. This is one of the most intense wildfire seasons in Canadian history due to extreme heat waves and record-breaking dry conditions.… pic.twitter.com/ubS7Gupgam —MarkJCarney Canadians "prefer to focus on helping one another," Minister of Energy and Natural Resources Tim Hodgson said during a media conference in Prince George, B.C., on Monday, referring to past assistance Canada has provided to fighting wildfires in the United States. "We want to focus on being good neighbours and good allies." The federal government is doing "what we can do" to combat wildfires, he said, outlining measures to train new firefighters, procure more water bombers, support the provinces in delivering emergency services and develop new firefighting technologies. "Extreme weather is a global challenge and we have to recognize that we're doing our part by trying to be a clean and conventional energy superpower," he said. "The world will be better off if we all work together as opposed to pointing fingers at one another." During a wildfire briefing in Toronto on Monday, Ontario Premier Doug Ford described Trump's comments as "disappointing to say the least." Smoke from wildfires in northwestern Ontario blanketed Toronto last week. (Cole Burston/The Canadian Press) "With all the assets the U.S. has, he's sitting there complaining," Ford said. "Why don't you send up some water bombers? Why don't you start helping us, like we would help you in a heartbeat? "You should support your neighbours. That's my message to the president." On Friday, Ford reminded the U.S. president, and other Republican legislators, it was time to repay the efforts Canada undertook to restore electricity in the U.S. after Hurricane Helene in 2024 and the California wildfires last year. "If there's some politicians out there chirping away, well maybe what you should do rather than complain is send support, send help, because we have done the exact same thing for our American friends. That's what you're supposed to do," Ford said. The premier said he thinks Americans are good neighbours but need to start acting that way. U.S. senator proposes sanctions Last week, Ohio Republican Sen. Bernie Moreno promised to introduce new legislation to sanction Canada for what his office called the "wildfire pollution emergency." The text of that bill, the Canada Fire Act, posted on Moreno's website, gives Trump the power to declare if smoke originating from Canada over the last 12 months found its way into the U.S. WATCH | Ford on wildfire comments from U.S. officials: 'Rubbish': Ontario premier responds to Trump's wildfire tariff threat | Duration 3:51 U.S. President Donald Trump raised the possibility of imposing punitive tariffs over Canadian wildfire smoke crossing the border. Ontario Premier Doug Ford called Trump's words a 'bunch of rubbish,' and pointed to wildfires burning in the U.S. If so declared, the bill, which has yet to be introduced to the Senate, sets out stiff financial penalties for any Canadian official, from the prime minister to lower-level officials, involved in wildfire management. Those penalties include halting loans to entities owned or controlled by the Canadian government, stopping any imports to the U.S. of anything produced by a Canadian government-owned entity and banning any officials from entering the U.S. if they have a hand in the wildfire response. As an interim measure, the legislation asks U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio to consider kicking out Canada's ambassador, chief of mission and more than a dozen other officials right down to the embassy spokesperson.

World.title: Scale of Calgary-wide search for missing 11-year-old boy 'very rare,' police say, as search enters 5th day
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results. As the search for a missing 11-year-old boy entered its fifth day on Monday, Calgary police said the scale of the city-wide search is "very rare," with hundreds of officers and volunteers involved. At a news conference on Monday, police said roughly 500 people have assisted with the search, covering approximately 6,500 kilometres. "This is absolutely not typical for a missing person file," Calgary police acting Staff Sgt. Scott Guterson said. "Searches of this degree are very, very rare in Calgary." Guterson asked the public to continue checking their yards, garages, open vehicles, RVs, sheds, pools or anywhere else a child would go. "We're going to keep hoping that he is alive, and we're going to keep acting as if he is alive, to bring him home as soon as humanly possible." Police released new CCTV footage of the boy they say was captured Thursday at 12:34 p.m. from a business adjacent to McKnight Boulevard and Centre Street N.W. The video was captured prior to previously released footage, Guterson said, in hopes that it will aid with the search. WATCH | Police release new CCTV footage of missing 11-year-old Calgary boy: Police release new CCTV footage of missing 11-year-old Calgary boy | Duration 2:26 On the fifth day searching for Parker, police released a video of the boy recorded Thursday at a business in the area of Centre Street N.W. and McKnight Boulevard. Investigators also gave an update on the scope of the search. As of Monday, police have received and assessed 150 tips from the public, and are reviewing more than 100 hours of CCTV, residential security camera and dashcam footage. Police are asking anyone with information about Parker's location, or who may have CCTV or dashcam footage, to call 403-266-1234 or reach the police's evidence submission portal. When he went missing on Thursday, Parker was seen shirtless, wearing grey shorts, black Skechers shoes and black noise-cancelling headphones. He’s four feet 11 inches tall and weighs approximately 90 pounds, with brown hair and brown eyes. Guterson said Parker is autistic and functions at a two- or three-year-old level. An undated photo of Parker shared by the Calgary Police Service. (Calgary Police Service) Police ask that any Calgarians choosing to search on their own do not interfere with police operations. They also ask any volunteer searchers to be mindful of the heat, so they do not end up requiring attention that could divert first responders from the search for Parker. Guterson advised the public that if they come across Parker, they should not engage him, but instead call police. He said they believe the boy is non-verbal, and gets agitated when strangers approach him. Police say Parker's family has expressed that he loves Disney music, so officers have been playing some of his favourite songs from patrol vehicles driving in search areas. We know Parker loves Disney music, so officers are playing some of his favourite songs from patrol vehicles in the search area in the hope that it may help draw his attention and encourage him to come out if he is nearby.

This search remains our highest priority. We'll continue… pic.twitter.com/kGAw6R7uMI —CalgaryPolice Child last seen on Thursday After Parker was seen Thursday at his day home in the 0 to 100 block of Connaught Drive N.W. between 11:08 and 11:41 a.m., the boy was seen in the Thorncliffe neighbourhood between 12:30 and 1 p.m., Guterson said. Clothing that’s believed to belong to Parker was found at noon Thursday in the 0 to 100 block of Northmount Drive N.W., police said. An emergency alert was broadcast on Saturday afternoon for Parker. Although police previously said the case did not meet the threshold for an Amber Alert, as foul play is not suspected, Calgary police said the provincial government made an exception in this case. "We are hopeful that expanding the awareness through the Alberta emergency system will generate new information that may help us locate him," said acting Insp. Rod MacNeil . On Saturday, police released a CCTV photo of the boy, captured when he was last seen on Thursday on the 5000-6000 block of Travis Crescent N.E., in hopes it might aid in the search. WATCH | More CCTV footage of Parker: CCTV footage of Parker, missing in Calgary | Duration 0:27 Footage released by the Calgary Police Service on July 19, shows missing 11-year-old, Parker, walking past a home on Travis Crescent N.E. on Thursday, July 16, 2026. On Sunday, police released additional CCTV footage of the boy taken at 12:52 p.m. Thursday in the 5500 block of Travis Crescent N.E. They had released a similar photo the day prior, in hopes it might help the search. Police also said Sunday that search efforts are being increasingly focused on areas connected to Parker's last known movements. Guterson said police know the boy likes water and part of their search has been to check whether he's near bodies of water. He said Parker tends to lock doors behind him, meaning people searching their properties should take the time to check behind doors even if they're locked. Family issues statement In a statement, Parker's family said they have been living "every parent's worst nightmare" since he went missing. "Every hour that passes without knowing where he is or whether he is safe has been incredibly difficult for us," the family said in its statement, sent out by CPS on their behalf shortly after Saturday afternoon's emergency alert. The family implored people to continue searching their properties for Parker. "Parker experiences the world in his own way. He may not respond when his name is called, and he can become frightened when approached by people he does not know," the family said. "Parker is deeply loved, and he is missed immensely. We just want our son home." An undated photo of Parker shared by the Calgary Police Service. (Calgary Police Service) CPS said it is aware of AI-generated, altered and unverified images of Parker or his whereabouts circulating online, and cautioned the public against viewing or sharing the content. "Unverified images, videos and claims can create confusion, spread misinformation and divert investigative resources away from credible leads that may assist in locating Parker," CPS said in a social media post on Monday. Situations like this warrant emergency alert, advocate says For Calgary mom Stephanie Karas, Saturday afternoon's emergency alert came far too late. "We've gotten alerts for tornadoes that have not touched down. We've gotten alerts for less, so I don't know why there wasn't," she said. Karas, a mother of two children with autism, says she's lobbying the municipal and provincial governments to create an emergency alert protocol specifically for situations like this. "Why isn't there something for vulnerable youth and adults that aren't equipped?" Karas said. WATCH | Why there are calls to expand Amber Alerts as police search for autistic Calgary boy: "It's long overdue, so somebody's got to start it," she said. "And if the people of Calgary have to start it and are motivated behind Parker, then that's what we'll do." MacNeil said Calgary police indicated to the province that "it may not be a true Amber Alert, but we need to reach as many Calgarians as we can in such a short amount of time." "The government stepped up right away, made that exception and we were able to get that alert out," he said. In a statement to CBC News, the provincial government said it "worked closely with CPS to assess the situation and determined that this measure to increase the public’s awareness of this missing child in these extremely particular circumstances was important."

World.title: Acclaimed Ontario art gallery to close for up to 3 years for redevelopment
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The McMichael Canadian Art Collection announced it will temporarily close to the public on the evening of July 26 to begin a landmark redevelopment of its building and grounds.

The art gallery — located in Kleinburg, Ont. — is the largest Canadian museum dedicated exclusively to Canadian and Indigenous art. Construction is expected to begin in fall 2026 and be completed in 2029.

Canadian firm Hariri Pontarini Architects leads the redevelopment, which marks the first major investment in the McMichael site in more than 40 years.

On its official website, the gallery describes "a transformative redevelopment — one that will enhance how we care for the collection, expand our exhibitions and programs, and improve the experience for every visitor who walks through our doors."

According to a news release, the project will add 60 per cent more space for exhibitions, education, conservation and public programming while modernizing outdated building systems and facilities.

It will also add state-of-the-art classrooms and studios, along with purpose-built spaces for events, concerts, lectures, conferences and dining.

The revitalization was announced in 2025 when the Ontario government pledged up to $50 million over three years to the project. The federal government committed an additional $25 million through its Green and Inclusive Community Buildings program.

The total cost of the project is estimated at $150 million and includes private donations.

During the construction period, much of the McMichael’s landmark collection will remain accessible through touring exhibitions of Canadian art across the country and abroad.

The permanent collection consists of almost 8,000 artworks, including masterworks by Tom Thomson, the Group of Seven and their contemporaries, as well as generations of Indigenous artists who have shaped and expanded the story of art in Canada, including Norval Morrisseau, Kent Monkman, Daphne Odjig and Jut-Ke-Nay Hazel Wilson.

A conceptual rendering of the lobby. (Hariri Pontarini Architects)

In a statement, the collection's chief curator Sarah Milroy said, "We are delighted to be embarking on this exciting voyage forward, giving Canadians the world-class museum that our rich culture deserves, from coast to coast to coast, and from past to present. The McMichael is the place where it all comes together."

The gallery, located on 40 hectares of wooded conservation land overlooking the East Humber River Valley, was once the private home of art collectors Robert and Signe McMichael.

In 1965, the McMichaels offered to donate their collection — as well as their home and land — to the Province of Ontario. On July 8, 1966, the "McMichael Conservation Collection of Art" officially opened to the public.

The McMichael cemetery is the final resting place for six members of the Group of Seven and the gallery's founders, Robert and Signe McMichael. (mcmichael.com)

The land also includes a small cemetery in a small patch of land bordered by trees and marked not by traditional gravestones, but large chunks of the Canadian Shield.

It is the final resting place for six members of the Group of Seven (Arthur Lismer, Frederick Varley, Lawren Harris, Frank Johnston, A.J. Casson and Jackson), four of the artists' spouses (Esther Lismer, Bess Harris, Margaret Petry and Florence Johnston) and the gallery's founders, Robert and Signe McMichael.

World.title: Despite the war, the U.S. and Iran are working together to deport asylum seekers, lawsuit says
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

LISTEN | Interview with immigration attorney Cyrus Mehri : As It Happens 6:30 U.S. shares asylum seekers' information with the Iranian regime, lawsuit claims

Even as the U.S. waged war with Iran and encouraged its citizens to take to the streets, the Trump administration was working with the regime to fast-track the deportations of dissidents, according to a new lawsuit.

Since March 2025, the U.S. government has been sharing the personal details of asylum seekers' cases with the Iranian regime, according to the suit filed earlier this month by the left-leaning Public Citizen Litigation Group and the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund (ALDF).

It alleges the U.S. government has welcomed regime officials into U.S. immigration detention centres to intimidate Iranians into returning to a country where they could face imprisonment, torture or death.

"We have a tradition of trying to be a beacon of hope for those fleeing political persecution and religious persecution, and we betrayed those confidences," Connecticut immigration attorney Cyrus Mehri, ALDF's co-founder, told As It Happens host Nil Kӧksal. "It just breaks my heart."

Detainees describe meetings with regime officials

The U.S. government has denied the allegations, which have not been proven in court.

But the ALDF says it has gathered multiple corroborating accounts that paint a stark picture of two seemingly enemy states working in collaboration against those fleeing persecution.

The non-profit has filed 11 sworn statements from Iranian asylum seekers in Customs and Enforcement (ICE) custody.

They include Christian converts, anti-regime protesters and 2SLGBTQ+ individuals who recounted being harassed, beaten, arrested and tortured by the Iranian regime.

WATCH | U.S.-Iran war escalations: Ship struck in Strait of Hormuz, U.S. announces another death as war escalates | Duration 7:16 The United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations says a vessel was struck by an unknown projectile in the Strait of Hormuz. The U.S. has also ramped up its strikes against Iran after announcing the death of a third service member over the weekend.

One woman said in her sworn statement that she was waiting in an Arizona detention facility for her asylum claim to be processed, when she and several other Iranian detainees were taken to a room to meet with a man described by ICE agents as an Iranian consular official.

"When I saw him, I felt cold," the woman, identified only as P.M., said in her hand-written declaration. "He looked like the regime guys."

The man had a list of the Iranian detainees' names, she wrote, and knew intricate details about their asylum claims, including information they had only disclosed to U.S. immigration officials.

S.O., another asylum seeker at the at the same Arizona facility, wrote in a sworn statement that the presence of an Iranian official spread fear among the Iranian asylum seekers.

"Many of us fled Iran to escape repression, political persecution or religious harassment," S.O. wrote. "His presence inside a U.S. detention facility was terrifying."

The asylum seekers all said the Iranian officials they met with urged them to sign documents agreeing to return to Iran.

Several said they were threatened with deportation to Africa if they declined to sign.

An inside source

Mehri says those first-hand accounts are backed up by details from a senior Iranian official who reached out to him in March 2026 to warn about a new immigration policy between the U.S. and Iran.

"Under this stark policy, the U.S. was seeking the help of the Islamic regime to get rid of people from Iran fleeing Iran that are lawfully knocking on the doors of America," Mehri said.

The lawsuit does not name the official who spoke with Mehri, but says he works with the Iranian Interests Section of the Pakistani Embassy in Washington, D.C., which provides de facto consular and diplomatic services between the Iran and the U.S.

The source claimed the two governments held monthly meetings to share information about hundreds of asylum cases. These meetings, the lawsuit says, were followed by several mass deportation flights to Iran, as reported by New York Times .

"I specifically asked him, 'Did the United States government institute protocols or get assurances for the safety of Woman Life Freedom protesters, pro-democracy protesters?' " Mehri said. "The answer was no."

Nor were there any procedures in place to protect Christian or 2SLGBTQ+ Iranians, he said.

The meetings stopped before Feb. 28, when war broke out between Iran and the U.S., the lawsuit says.

But even as the conflict raged on, the lawsuit alleges ICE has "continued to mail or hand deliver document packages to the Iranian Interests Section."

"Don't forget, we're at war with Iran. Why are we turning over asylum seekers to Iran on a silver platter?" Mehri said. "It seems like the U.S. government and Iranian government can't seem to agree on anything, except for this."

The lawsuit names U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio as a defendant. The U.S. State Department did not respond to a request for comment. (Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images)

Suit wants halt on sharing info with Iran

The lawsuit, filed in Federal District Court in Washington, D.C., names ICE, U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio and the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) as defendants.

DHS, which oversees ICE, has denied any wrongdoing.

“These allegations that ICE shared asylum application records with the Iranian government are FALSE," a DHS spokesperson told CBC in an email.

“ICE is committed to ensuring that illegal aliens are informed of their right to communicate with their consular representatives. Consistent with established protocols, ICE provides illegal aliens the opportunity to contact their consular post and facilitates consular access to detained individuals, in accordance with applicable laws, regulations, and agency policy."

The State Department did not respond to a request for comment.

The lawsuit calls on the U.S. government to immediately halt information sharing with Iran, to disclose to any current asylum seekers if their privacy has been compromised and to cease the mass deportation of Iranians.

"This has to end immediately," Mehri said. "America is better than this."

World.title: Who is Nolan Wells, and why has the Black Mississippi teen's death received widespread attention?
World.content:
The audio version of this article is generated by AI-based technology. Mispronunciations can occur. We are working with our partners to continually review and improve the results.

The death of Nolan Wells, a Black teenager whose body was located on an island off the Mississippi coast after he spent the Fourth of July there with three white friends, has drawn widespread attention amid an ongoing investigation and mounting unanswered questions.

Family and supporters of the 18-year-old gathered in a Mississippi church Monday to mourn and celebrate him.

Wells's death, which has prompted an outpouring of reactions online — largely fuelled by questions about race in the U.S. — captured national attention and prompted calls for an independent investigation. Here's what we know about the case and why it has garnered so much online attention:

Who is Nolan Wells?

Wells, described by his parents as having a big heart, would have turned 19 next month.

The ceremony on Monday began with tearful remarks from Wells's parents, who described their son as a warm and gentle presence, a gifted athlete and a role model to his younger siblings.

"He had a way of making people feel seen, welcomed and valued," said Christine Wonsley, the teenager's mother. "He could lift your confidence with just a few words and make you feel like you belong."

Wells's parents, Christine and Elmore Wonsley, attend a news conference in Manhattan on July 10. (David 'Dee' Delgado/Reuters)

Wells attended Southwest Mississippi Community College, where he played wide receiver on the football team.

His father, Elmore Wonsley, described him as a "silent leader" among his teammates and friends, adding that he was able to make friends anywhere he went.

"He was focused on what he wanted. He wanted to make life better for his family," he told GMA. "He wanted to have his own family."

Prior to the funeral, relatives filed into at Center Pointe Church in Ocean Springs, Miss., for a visitation period on Monday, featuring gospel singers and a photo slideshow in which Wells was often grinning and decked out in football gear.

What do we know about his death?

Wells travelled to Horn Island with a group of friends on July 4 but failed to return with them when they left around 3 p.m.

Conflicting accounts have been given as to whether he planned to remain on Horn Island, about 11 kilometres offshore, or return with his friends.

The roughly 17-kilometre-long spit of land is near the Alabama state line. The island is uninhabited and accessible only by boat, officials said, and is popular for parties and gatherings.

His mother reported him missing shortly after midnight.

The next day, boat and rescue crews launched searches and his body was recovered in waters on the northwestern tip of Horn Island.

Wells poses with his parents in an undated photo. (Ben Crump Law/Handout/Reuters)

Authorities with the Jackson County Sheriff's Department and other agencies were quick to say they did not suspect foul play. Results of an official autopsy are still pending, and the investigation is continuing, officials say.

Sheriff John Ledbetter has said Wells's friends are co-operating with the investigation. He said initial interviews suggested Wells chose to stay on the island and that his friends believed he would get a ride with someone else.

Both the family's attorneys and sheriff's department investigators have asked witnesses or anyone with video from the island to come forward as they seek answers about the moments before his disappearance and death.

There are many troubling questions about the case, civil rights attorney Ben Crump said at a news conference on July 10 in New York with civil rights leader Rev. Al Sharpton and Wells's parents. Crump represents the family and is aiding an independent investigation, including a private autopsy.

The main question, according to Crump, is the discrepancy between what Wells's friends said and what a young woman they met on the island said.

The three friends who travelled with Wells to the island said Wells told them he wanted to stay there with the young woman when they left the afternoon of July 4, per Crump, but she has said that Wells got on the boat with the boys. Crump also said that videos circulating online allegedly show Wells in a heated argument with his friends.

Also raising suspicions, Crump said, is that Wells's phone was found not with his body, but in the possession of one of the young men who had accompanied him to Horn Island. Wells's mother tracked it down using Life360, a location-sharing app, and she said it appears that several social media messages had been deleted.

His parents said their son was an avid Snapchat user, but there were no posts or messages from the 24 hours or so before they retrieved it.

Why has his death received so much public attention?

For some Black Americans, the case has sparked painful discussions about navigating predominantly white spaces and racism, while civil rights leaders and others have renewed longstanding concerns about disparities in attention to missing persons cases involving Black victims.

Speculation and suspicion about the teen's death have been rampant online, as people grapple with the state's history of racial tension and what it means to be a Black person in a majority-white space.

Family and attorneys have said photos and videos of the Fourth of July celebration on the island, where nearly 200 people had gathered, suggest that Wells was one of very few Black people present.

The Congressional Black Caucus also echoed calls for an independent investigation into the death.

CBC News reached out, but did not receive further comment from the sheriff’s office.

Filmmaker and actor Spike Lee attends the July 10 news conference regarding Wells's death. (David 'Dee' Delgado/Reuters)

Actor and producer Tyler Perry is helping pay for Wells's funeral. Former NFL quarterback Colin Kaepernick is helping pay for an independent autopsy, and filmmaker Spike Lee attended a news conference last week in support of Wells's family.

In a fiery eulogy Monday, Sharpton promised a $50,000 US reward for any new information about the circumstances around Wells's death. He invoked the history of racist violence in Mississippi, including the lynching of Emmett Till and assassination of American civil rights leader Medgar Evers.

"The reason why a lot of people in the nation are looking at this Nolan situation is that we've looked at history in Mississippi. Some of us remember what happened in Mississippi," Sharpton said, to loud applause in the church.

"Before we can medicate and heal today, we've got to look at your history."

What happens next?

Wells’s family has launched its own investigation into his death and commissioned an independent autopsy, saying the information they have received from authorities doesn’t add up.

Crump said the family's attorneys agreed to work with the local district attorney investigating Wells's death to inspect the contents of his cellphone.

He added that the district attorney committed to presenting the investigation, which is separate from the family's independent investigation, to a grand jury once it's complete. A grand jury is typically comprised of 15 to 25 citizens who listen to the prosecutor's evidence and decide whether there is enough evidence for an indictment.

"The hope is when this is presented to the grand jury, all relevant witnesses and evidence will be presented to them, so we can have a fair and impartial investigation into the death of Nolan Wells," Crump said.

"Our lived experiences tell us that we must question everything, everybody's role, law enforcement's role. That is the lived experience as Black people in America."

World.title: Petro calls for “peaceful resistance” against Colombia’s incoming “viceroyalty”
World.content:
President Gustavo Petro called on the people to “prepare peaceful resistance” to the “viceroyalty” that “has been imposed as the president of Colombia.”

During an Independence Day speech in the poor south of Bogota, Petro told thousands of supporters that “the next president of Colombia will be a servant to the rulers of the United States who helped him ‘get elected’.”

“We move from the status of a republic to the status of a viceroyalty again, just like 216 years ago,” said Petro, who on Sunday accepted to become the political leader of the leftist opposition.

It is time to give the second cry of independence… Shout freedom and resistance! Gustavo Petro

Rather than a repetition of the 1810 revolution, the outgoing president proposed to “prepare for peaceful resistance” in defense of communities who benefited from the government’s reforms.

How do you repeal the decree on hourly work that ends the labor reform that created stability, a vital wage, and better working conditions? How? Well, with a permanent general strike of millions of working men and women in Colombia! It is not just by shouting, it is not just by raising flags, they are already used to that… No, it is with a production strike, which is permitted by the National Constitution of Colombia, it is a universal right! And that indeed is civil disobedience! If they are going to strike down the stabilities, the working conditions achieved in this government, a general and indefinite strike in Colombia! Gustavo Petro

Petro threatened to “surround the centers of illegitimate power in Colombia until legitimacy exists once again, which can only be achieved through free popular decision without algorithms, and without foreign money.”

To protect the people, the president suggested the creation of unarmed “liberatory guards” that work in a network, “because they want to kill.”

Wherever they touch a neighborhood, wherever they touch a peasant estate, the network must summon solidarity, it must become a demonstration of all adjacent neighborhoods, of all adjacent villages, of the whole country if necessary. Gustavo Petro

“The only way to stop fascism,” said Petro, “is in peace. It is with joy, but it is with millions and millions of Colombian men and women.”

World.title: Petro to assume political leadership of Colombia’s leading leftist party
World.content:
President Gustavo Petro said Sunday that he would become the leader of Colombia’s largest political party on the left, the Historic Pact.

In a tweet, Petro responded to Senator Ivan Cepeda, who proposed him as party president at a political rally in the city of Tunja on Saturday.

Petro said he would “accept the proposal of my party after surrendering power to the far-right President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella.

The president said he would first go “on a vacation I deserve and didn’t have during four years of governance.”

We will work toward peace and social justice and for a national agreement that prevents violent confrontation among Colombians, and we will seek to contribute to the democratic stability of the countries that Simon Bolívar liberated. President Gustavo Petro

The Historic Pact party was formed in March from a coalition of multiple parties that have long supported the political careers of Petro and Cepeda.

Following a significant electoral victory, the party became the largest of Colombia and will assume 25 of 103 seats in the Senate.

Petro’s former party, Colombia Humana, contributed 12 senators to the collective.

The president started his political career while being a member of the M-19 guerrilla group, which demobilized in 1990.

Petro was elected to the House of Representatives in 1998 an became a senator in 2006.

Between 2012 and 2015, the president was mayor of the capital Bogota.

Petro has been the most popular and powerful leftist politician since the violent death of Liberal Party leader Jorge Eliecer Gaitan in 1948, and was sanctioned by the US Government amid his opposition to the genocide in Gaza.

The president has insisted that his successor won the June elections through fraud and has refused to recognize De la Espriella as his successor.

World.title: Colombia’s peace and human rights offices to close: De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella announced on Monday that he will close the Peace Commissioner’s Office, which was in charge of negotiating peace and implementing peace deals with illegal armed groups.

“The Office of the Peace Commissioner is coming to an end, because there will be no more sham peace processes during my administration,” said De la Espriella in his weekly address to the nation that was broadcast on his social media platforms.

According to the far-right president-elect, who will take office on August 7, other presidential commissioners that will disappear are those of National Reconciliation. and the Office of Human Rights and International Humanitarian Law.

The functions of these offices will be taken over by the Interior, Foreign and Defense ministries that, according to De la Espriella, have been doubling the work of the presidential commissioners.

“These are functions that, by law, are already carried out by other ministries,” so the government can “avoid duplication and extra costs,” said the president-elect.

De la Espriella seems keen to abruptly end the peace policy of his predecessor, President Gustavo Petro, for being too lenient to illegal armed groups.

The president-elect also promised to close war crimes tribunal JEP, which has been trying thousands of former guerrillas and former members of the military.

De la Espriella could only do this through legislation that would change the constitution and the international treaties that protect the victims of an armed conflict between the State and the now-defunct guerrilla organization FARC.

World.title: Petro to seek court order to annul election of De la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s President Gustavo Petro said Tuesday that he will seek a court order to annul the election of President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella.

In a post on social media platform X, Petro said he had gather enough evidence to prove that his successor “was elected from abroad, with nonexistent votes.”

“Today we are presenting the body of evidence we have gathered to the representatives elected by the people, and we will file a lawsuit with the courts to annul the elections, as is our duty,” said the outgoing president.

We are not making things up when we say that Abelardo’s government was elected from abroad, with nonexistent votes included in the percentage automatically adjusted by algorithms created by private Israeli companies with the endorsement of their genocidal government. President Gustavo Petro

“We are facing not only the imminent rise of fascism in Colombia but also what may be the greatest threat to global democracy since Hitler’s time,” said Petro.

In a response that was broadcast on his social media channels, De la Espriella reiterated that Petro was a “tyrant” who was trying to perpetuate power through a coup d’etat with the help of the leftist runner-up in the election, Senator Ivan Cepeda.

Even before becoming a candidate, I warned you: Petro is a tyrant in the making who seeks to perpetuate himself in power by any means necessary. And today, as the president-elect of all of you, I ratify what I have said for so many years. This is no longer an analysis or an opinion; it is a palpable reality. From the moment nearly 13 million Colombians stood by me to defeat him and his political frontman, Petro and Cepeda began their Plan B to stay in power, no matter what it takes. And they want to do so through a coup d’état. President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella

The president-elect asked the armed forces “to protect the Constitution and democracy, and to disobey any order that Petro may be giving to the contrary.”

Resistance, dear compatriots. We cannot allow them to snatch away what we achieved at the ballot box in an epic democratic battle this past June 21. Let us resist, for August 7 is near. God, the vote, and democracy have spoken; we are going to defend the Constitution and the rule of law as we must. President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella

De la Espriella has long claimed that he will extradite his predecessor to the United States.

World.title: De la Espriella suspends Colombia’s transfer of power
World.content:
President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella on Tuesday suspended the transfer of power after President Gustavo Petro accused him of fraud.

In a post on social media platform X, De la Espriella said he had “given instructions to the vice president-elect of the Republic to immediately suspend the handover process with the corrupt government that is ending its term.”

I have just given instructions to the president-elect of the Republic to immediately suspend the handover process with the corrupt government that is ending its term, a government that, with its decisions and its conduct, seeks to destroy Colombia. Abelardo de la Espriella

“My duty is to protect the interests of the Nation and guarantee a serious, transparent transition at the service of Colombians, never to legitimize the disaster or the disregard for the constitutional order,” said the president-elect.

In a press conference, Finance Minister German Avila said that he had also suspended cooperation with the transition process in response to comments made by a member of De la Espriella’s team, convicted fraudster Carlos ALonso Lucio, that “undermine the respect, dignity, and decency” of the transition process.

Recent statements by members of the incoming transition committee undermine the respect, dignity, and decency of a process such as the one we are carrying out. These statements were surely made intentionally to hinder the transition process. Accusations and insults have been leveled against the president and his administration, alleging that they are criminals, that they are manipulating the justice system, and that they are seeking to extradite us, among other blunders that have been made. German Avila

“All we have received are insults and disrespect, slander and offenses, and we will not tolerate a single further act of aggression or threat,” said the finance minister.

Avila asked Inspector General Gregorio Eljach to oversee the continuation of the process.

In a post on social media platform X, incoming vice-President Jose Manuel Restrepo stressed that his team would continue going through the books to make sure that “those who have betrayed the trust of the Colombian people must answer to the institutions and to history.”

World.title: Colombia’s Petro refuses to recognize successor Abelardo de la Espriella
World.content:
Colombia’s outgoing President Gustavo Petro said Monday that he doesn’t recognize the outcome of the election that made the far-right Abelardo de la Espriella president-elect.

In a post on social media platform X, Petro said he saw “evidence of electoral fraud carried out through algorithms and with foreign funding, which is prohibited by our Constitution.”

The president called the alleged election fraud “the harshest blow to national sovereignty since the Spanish reconquest during the years of the Patria Boba.”

Colombia’s president, according to the decision of the Colombians, is the philosopher Iván Cepeda. We have suffered the harshest blow to national sovereignty since the Spanish reconquest during the years of the “Patria Boba.” President Gustavo Petro

According to Petro, he had “all the information about how, from an IP server located in Los Angeles, California, owned by the Bautista brothers, integrated into the scrutiny operation, algorithms were used that substantially varied the vote in favor of” De la Espriella.

Additionally, the president accused a close associate of US President Donald Trump, Florida attorney Dan Newlin, of paying a $1.8 million Facebook campaign for De la Espriella.

In a post that was published on Sunday, Petro asked De la Espriella of he had registered the alleged campaign contribution of Trump’s former ambassador pick.

In a response, Newlin said that “I have contributed zero dollars, not a single cent, directly or indirectly, to his campaign.”

“I challenge you to provide evidence to the Colombian people to support these demonstrably false accusations. You will not be able to do so, because no such contribution ever occurred,” said the Florida attorney.

Petro has been promoting conspiracy theories about alleged election fraud ever since the June 21 elections that were won by De la Espriella with a 250,000-vote difference.

World.title: Colombia’s land agency claims elections triggered surge in land theft
World.content:
The director of Colombia’s land agency ANT filed criminal complaints about at least eight attempts to steal land from beneficiaries of President Gustavo Petro’s land reform.

According to ANT director Harman Felipe, armed men associated with drug traffickers and paramilitary commanders intimidated the communities at six plots that had been given to victim of the armed conflict.

The incidents we have reported follow the same pattern of intimidation against families who have benefited from the Agrarian Reform. The threats are intended to force communities to leave so that land currently in the hands of small farmers can be reclaimed. What is at stake is not only the safety of these families, but also the defense of the Agrarian Reform and the right of small farmers to remain on their land. Harman Felipe

In one of the attempts, armed land thieves allegedly tortured members of a family that had been given land in Puerto Lopez, a municipality in the central Meta province.

This land used to belong to Ignacio Alvarez, a drug trafficker of the now-defunct Norte del Valle cartel.

Most incidents happened in the Magdalena Medio region, where the legal occupants of five plots were ordered to abandon their properties by armed men.

At one of the plots, which used to be of Daniel Barrera, the owners were told “these lands don’t belong to guerrillas.”

At another plot, a member of the Isaza Clan threatened a women’s association that was given control over land that used to belong to Maria Georgina Arango, the wife of a former commander of paramilitary organization AUC, Ovidio Isaza, a.k.a. “Roque.”

In Cordoba, a Caribbean province, the legal occupants of another one of Alvarez’s plots fled.

“We want the Attorney General’s Office to investigate these incidents, which are not minor matters and could even constitute crimes against humanity due to the displacement they have caused,” the ANT director told press.

Land thieves stole between 6.5 and 8 million hectares of land during the armed conflict between 1964 and 2016, often with the support of corrupt elements within the State.

World.title: Cepeda calls for civil disobedience if De la Espriella doesn’t renounce US citizenship
World.content:
Opposition leader Ivan Cepeda urged followers to exercise civil disobedience unless President-elect Abelardo de la Espriella does not renounce his US citizenship and ends the persecution of opponents in the US.

At a press conference, Cepeda announced the “civil disobedience against the violation of our national dignity” and called on the 12.7 million Colombians who voted for him to follow his lead.

The leftist opposition leader said that he would “not lend myself to this violation of our sovereignty and will embark on the path of peaceful civil disobedience”

“This implies refusing to recognize the authority of someone who does not answer to the defense of national sovereignty. Let it be very clear: peaceful civil disobedience,” said Cepeda.

I call upon and invite the millions of voters who placed their trust in me to do the same and, if what I demand is not met, to peacefully ignore any order, provision, or mandate from someone who does not fulfill the role of guardian and guarantor of our Political Constitution. As civil disobedience teaches us, when the law, institutions, or authority come into conflict with moral conscience, the citizen has not only the right but the duty to resist peacefully, refusing to collaborate with injustice, opprobrium, or oppression. Ivan Cepeda

In order to call off the civil disobedience, the opposition leader demanded that De la Espriella renounce his US citizenship and clarified whether or not he is an agent or an asset of US intelligence agencies like the DEA and CIA.

Additionally, Cepeda demanded that the president-elect “cease all persecution against President Gustavo Petro and drop any attempt to extradite him,” and end the persecution of political opponents.

De la Espriella announced on Sunday that he had called on his transition team to send evidence of alleged wrongdoing by the Petro administration to Colombian justice and the US Department of Justice “so that they can determine what their competitive processes are, because there’s an international conspiracy going on there.”

The president-elect has long vowed to extradite his predecessor.

World.title: Chile’s Municipalities, Senapred Meet Ahead of Storm Forecast
World.content:
SANTIAGO, Chile â As Chile prepares for an approaching winter storm system, the Association of Municipalities of Chile (Amuch) held a high-level coordination meeting with the National Disaster Prevention and Response Service (Senapred) to strengthen municipal emergency response measures.

The discussions focused on improving collaboration among municipalities, national agencies, and private service providers to better protect residents during severe weather events.

Power Companies Face Pressure Over Response Times

A central topic in the meeting was the performance of electric utilities during past emergencies. JosÃ© Manuel Palacios, mayor of La Reina, expressed concern over delayed responses from power companies in recent years.

âWe are exploring ways, together with Senapred and other institutions, to develop more efficient actions and hold the companies accountable to meet the response times our residents need,â Palacios said.

Rural Water Supply Risks Tied to Electricity

For rural municipalities, electrical outages pose a dual threat, as potable water systems often rely on electric power. Paula GÃ¡rate, mayor of Melipilla, emphasized the heightened vulnerability of rural areas during storms.

âLosing electricity also means losing access to potable water. Many rural water systems depend on electricity, and that remains our greatest concern,â GÃ¡rate noted.

Coordinated Municipal Efforts to Mitigate Risks

Senapred Director Alicia CebriÃ¡n highlighted the essential role of municipal governments in both preparation and response phases.

âMunicipalities play a crucial role in coordination, information gathering, and implementing mitigation works to reduce the impact of winter threats on residents,â CebriÃ¡n stated.

She underscored that emergency prevention and mitigation is a shared responsibility across public agencies and institutions. âPublic authorities who are directly involved in disaster management bear this responsibility, and we are committed to fulfilling it,â she added.

Winter System Expected to Test Emergency Readiness

The coordination meeting comes as Chileâs central regions brace for a frontal system expected to bring heavy rain and strong winds. Authorities emphasized that ongoing preparation and inter-agency cooperation will be key to minimizing disruption and protecting vulnerable communities.

World.title: Brian Wilson, Legendary Beach Boys Co-Founder, Dies at 82
World.content:
LOS ANGELES â Brian Wilson, the legendary musician, songwriter and co-founder of The Beach Boys, has died at the age of 82, his family announced.

“We are heartbroken to announce that our beloved father Brian Wilson has passed away,” the family said in a statement. “We are at a loss for words right now. Please respect our privacy at this time as our family is grieving. We realize that we are sharing our grief with the world.”

Born in 1942 in Hawthorne, California, Wilson formed The Beach Boys in 1961 with his younger brothers Carl and Dennis, cousin Mike Love, and friend Al Jardine. The band became one of the most influential and commercially successful acts in music history, selling over 100 million records worldwide.

Wilson was the creative force behind the groupâs distinctive harmonies and groundbreaking studio sound. His 1966 album Pet Sounds is regarded as a masterpiece that reshaped the boundaries of pop music production.

Among The Beach Boys’ many hits, Wilson co-wrote and produced I Get Around, Help Me, Rhonda, and Good Vibrations. Rolling Stone ranked The Beach Boys 12th on its list of the “100 Greatest Artists of All Time.”

Tributes poured in following news of his death. Nancy Sinatra shared a photo with Wilson on Instagram, writing, âHis cherished music will live forever as he travels through the Universe and beyond. God bless you, sweet Brian.â

Sean Ono Lennon called Wilson the “American Mozart” and a “one of a kind genius from another world,” adding: âAnyone who really knows me knows how heartbroken I am about Brian Wilson passing. Not many people influenced me as much as he did. I feel very lucky that I was able to meet him and spend some time with him. He was always very kind and generous.”

Throughout his life, Wilson faced significant personal struggles. Diagnosed with paranoid schizophrenia in 1984, his condition was linked by doctors to earlier psychedelic drug use. In early 2024, his family revealed he had developed dementia.

Wilson’s wife, Melinda, with whom he shared 24 years of marriage and five adopted children, died earlier in 2024. He also had two daughters, Carnie and Wendy, from his first marriage.

Despite his health battles, Wilsonâs legacy remains unparalleled. His influence on songwriting, vocal harmony, and studio innovation continues to inspire generations of musicians.

World.title: Chile and Norway Deepen Antarctic Cooperation with New Agreement
World.content:
Chile and Norway signed a memorandum of understanding on Antarctic cooperation Monday, reinforcing their shared commitment to peace, science, and environmental protection in the region.

The agreement, signed by Chilean Foreign Minister Alberto van Klaveren and Norwegian Minister of International Development Ã smund GrÃ¸ver, aims to strengthen bilateral coordination under the Antarctic Treaty System. It outlines enhanced collaboration on scientific research, climate monitoring, and the preservation of marine ecosystems through frameworks such as the Antarctic Treaty Consultative Meetings and the Commission for the Conservation of Antarctic Marine Living Resources (CCAMLR).

The accord includes provisions for regular dialogue between scientific and governmental institutions in both countries and seeks to optimize joint efforts in Antarctic and sub-Antarctic research. Both nations also pledged support for the Polar Codeâs implementation, aiming to improve safety and environmental standards for ships operating in polar waters.

Operational and logistical cooperation between Chileâs and Norwayâs national Antarctic programs will also be explored, particularly in alignment with CCAMLRâs conservation objectives.

This renewed alliance builds on the long-standing historical ties between the two nations and reaffirms their role as active stewards of one of the worldâs most fragile and strategically vital environments.
