03 What moved it

The immediate driver of the softer tape is a modest dip in spot prices combined with visibly high inventories in China, where battery‑grade lithium carbonate has eased to about 151,500 yuan per tonne and traders report limited appetite for aggressive restocking. Seasonal production from Qinghai salt lakes, plus upgraded supply across Chinese spot markets, has bolstered availability, giving buyers more bargaining power and cooling day‑to‑day price momentum.

At the same time, global demand is no longer the one‑way street it looked like during the 2022 spike, with electric‑vehicle sales growth uneven across markets and battery makers signalling that they can afford to run down stocks before paying up again. Equity investors, looking at that combination of high inventories, seasonal supply and slightly softer spot prices, have chosen to trim positions in miners and ETFs for now, even though price‑forecast revisions by houses such as Fastmarkets still point to higher average prices in 2026 and 2027.

04 The Latin American read

For Latin America, and for foreign money eyeing the region, the key context is that the Lithium Triangle – Argentina, Bolivia and Chile – holds roughly 58–60% of global lithium resources and already provides around 35% of world supply. That geological endowment has turned salt flats like Salar de Atacama and Salar del Hombre Muerto into strategic assets, attracting an expected 30‑plus billion dollars of investment over about five years as Chinese, North American and Australian players race to lock in future production.

Monday’s price action does not change that structural picture, but it does highlight the region’s exposure to global cycles: when inventories build in China or futures prices pause, Triangle producers feel it via the tape. At the same time, the emphasis on water use, community rights and policy choices in Santiago, Buenos Aires and La Paz means that what investors are really reading into every move in SQM and peers is a blend of market signals and political risk across the Andes.

05 The names to watch

Albemarle remains one of the defining names for foreign investors trying to understand lithium, with a portfolio spanning US and Chilean brine assets and a share price that, despite the latest 2.14% dip to 118.20 dollars, still reflects strong year‑to‑date performance and robust margins at current price levels. Chile’s SQM, closing at 67.69 dollars down 3.04%, is the flagship Latin American producer inside the LIT basket, and its sharper decline underlines how Chilean policy debates over royalties, state participation and environmental standards can amplify market moves.

The ETF itself, LIT at 66.92 dollars down 2.14%, remains the simplest way for outsiders to gain diversified exposure to miners and battery‑tech names without picking individual stocks, but it will remain sensitive to shifts in sentiment toward China, EV demand and commodity equities as an asset class. Beyond these, investors are watching other Triangle developers and global producers benefiting from Zimbabwe’s export restrictions and delayed project restarts in China, which have helped push price forecasts for 2026 and 2027 higher even after this latest pause.

06 The outlook

Looking ahead, most credible forecasts still see lithium in a structurally tight position: prices for lithium carbonate are hovering around year‑to‑date highs near 25,156 dollars per tonne, long‑term projections have been revised up to about 23.80 dollars per kilogram for 2026, and demand from EVs and grid‑scale storage is expected to outpace new mine supply into the late 2020s. For Latin America’s Lithium Triangle, that suggests that short-term pullbacks in LIT, Albemarle and SQM are likely to be noise within a bigger story of rising investment, strategic importance and the crucial question of how quickly the region can turn vast resources into sustainable, socially accepted production – with Chinese inventories and local permitting decisions the variables to watch.

07 What to watch

Chinese inventories: Elevated lithium carbonate stocks in China are currently capping spot prices and shaping short-term equity sentiment; a move from accumulation to destocking would likely support a rebound in miners and LIT.

The pace at which new brine and hard‑rock projects in Argentina, Bolivia and Chile move from announcement to production will determine whether forecast supply deficits materialise or are eased. Growth in electric‑vehicle sales and battery energy‑storage deployments across the Americas and Asia remains the main pull factor for lithium; any meaningful slowdown or policy change would quickly feed through to prices. Policy and social licence: Regulatory changes, royalty regimes and community responses in Chile, Argentina and Bolivia will affect both costs and timelines for new capacity, making local governance a key risk for foreign investors.

Is LIT a direct play on lithium prices?

No, LIT is an equity ETF holding lithium miners and battery‑technology companies, so its price reflects investor sentiment toward those shares and not the spot lithium carbonate price itself.

Why did lithium miners fall if spot prices barely moved?

Miners dropped on the latest session mainly because of high inventories, seasonal supply from Chinese salt lakes and profit‑taking after a strong year, even though spot prices only eased by around 0.20–0.33%.

How important is the Lithium Triangle for global supply?

The Lithium Triangle of Argentina, Bolivia and Chile holds about 58–60% of global lithium resources and currently produces roughly a third of world output, making it central to long‑term supply and price formation.

What drives most lithium demand today?

Electric vehicles already account for roughly 63–70% of lithium demand, with grid‑scale energy storage emerging as a second major pillar, so transport and power‑system electrification are the main drivers of the market.

03 What moved it

The immediate catalyst is the tightening supply picture centred on Latin America. The International Copper Study Group has reversed its 2026 market forecast from a 209,000-tonne surplus to a 150,000-tonne deficit as mine delays and accidents in Chile and Peru curtail output, and some industry analysis suggests the real shortfall could be nearer 330,000 tonnes once refinery constraints and the permanent closure of Cobre Panamá, which had produced about 350,000 tonnes per year, are included.

On the demand side, copper is being repriced as a long-term energy-transition input. S&P Global expects global copper demand to double by 2035, driven by electric vehicles, clean power generation and grid expansion, while EVs and artificial-intelligence data centres are projected to account for more than half of copper demand by 2040 in some scenarios, gradually reshaping copper from a traditional construction metal into a structural growth commodity.

04 The Latin American read

Latin America sits at the centre of the global copper story. Chile remains the world’s largest producer, with about 5.3 million metric tons of mine output in 2024 and roughly 23–24% of global production, and it holds the largest copper reserves at approximately 190 million metric tons, while Peru, now ranking third behind the Democratic Republic of the Congo on some measures, still contributes about 2.6 million metric tons annually.

Together, Chile and Peru supply roughly 40% of global mined copper, and the wider Latin American region accounts for about 45% of world output, which means any labour stoppage, regulatory change or infrastructure bottleneck there propagates almost instantly into futures prices. For foreign investors, this concentration makes copper a proxy for Latin American risk and opportunity: on one hand, an estimated 246 billion dollars could flow into regional copper projects by 2050, while on the other, events such as the August 2025 tunnel collapse at Codelco’s El Teniente mine show how quickly supply expectations can be upset.

05 The names to watch

Southern Copper, closing at 175.07 dollars with a 1.50% daily gain, is a direct avenue for global investors to access Peruvian and Mexican copper assets, and its share price often trades as much on regional political sentiment as on the underlying metal. The company’s fortunes are tied to stability and regulatory clarity in Peru and Mexico, so its equity performance acts as a barometer of how comfortable international money feels with Latin America’s policy trajectory in a market that is tightening.

Freeport-McMoRan, headquartered in the United States but among the world’s largest listed copper miners, closed at 58.79 dollars, a 0.70% gain on the day that reinforces its role as a global copper bellwether. Analysts tracked by Investing.com point to a consensus 12-month price target near 70.93 dollars and an overall Buy rating, signalling that institutional investors see the current copper environment as an opportunity. Meanwhile, CPER at 38.42 dollars offers the cleanest listed vehicle to track copper futures alone, without the company-level risks embedded in miner equities.

06 The outlook

The forward-looking picture is one of sustained tension between tight supply and structurally rising demand. On the supply side, ICSG data and industry analysis point to a real and persistent deficit in 2026, with spillovers from mine delays and closures likely to keep inventories under pressure unless new projects in Chile, Peru and elsewhere advance from planning to production faster than currently expected. On the demand side, energy transition investments, electric vehicles and AI-driven data centres underpin a secular rise in copper consumption, while China’s share of global demand is expected to ease gradually as the United States and India step up, broadening demand sources and potentially moderating the commodity’s traditional boom-bust cycles.

07 What to watch

Latin American mine execution: Because Chile and Peru supply about 40% of global mined copper, project delays, labour disputes or safety incidents there can quickly tighten the market and push futures and miners higher, making operational updates from Codelco, Southern Copper and Freeport-McMoRan’s regional assets essential reading.

China’s copper demand indicators: China still produces over 45% of refined copper and imports around 60% of global copper ore, so its manufacturing, property and stimulus data remain critical price drivers even as new demand centres emerge in the United States and India.

Energy transition and grid spending: Forecasts that copper demand will double by 2035, driven by electric vehicles, clean power generation and grid upgrades, mean that green-infrastructure policy decisions in the United States, Europe and Asia will shape the medium-term price path more than short-term factory data.

Investment flows into Latin American projects: With Latin America expected to attract around 246 billion dollars of copper-related investment by 2050, monitoring how quickly capital is committed and how smoothly projects advance in Chile and Peru will indicate whether the projected supply gap can be closed.

Frequently Asked Questions

Is Chile still the number one copper producer?

Yes. Chile remains the world’s largest copper producer, with around 5.3 million metric tons of mine output in 2024 and roughly 23–24% of global production, and it also holds the largest copper reserves at about 190 million metric tons.

Where does Peru rank among global copper producers?

Peru produces about 2.6 million metric tons of copper per year and is generally ranked as the third-largest copper miner globally, although recent data place the Democratic Republic of the Congo in second position ahead of Peru.

Why does CPER not mirror spot copper prices exactly?

CPER tracks copper futures contracts, not spot transactions, meaning its net asset value follows the settlement prices of futures on exchanges such as COMEX rather than the physical spot market where copper is immediately delivered, which can cause divergence especially during periods of speculative activity.

How important is China to the copper market today?

China remains central, producing over 45% of the world’s refined copper and importing about 60% of global copper ore, but forecasts suggest its share of global copper consumption will gradually decline by 2030 as demand in the United States and India rises, making copper less of a single-country story over time.

This quiet but telling divergence came as the US dollar firmed on safe-haven demand and Treasury yields stayed elevated, a combination that tends to cap gold’s upside but does not always prevent silver from rallying when industrial and speculative flows line up. For foreign investors looking at Latin America, the moves matter less for their size than for what they signal about how global markets are balancing fear, growth hopes and the region’s role in supplying the world’s silver.

Silver’s more confident rise hints that investors are willing to take on slightly more risk where industrial demand and tight supply from top producers like Mexico and Peru can still underpin price, even if the broader macro picture remains unsettled. The interpretive verdict is that precious metals are waiting for a clearer signal from US policy and inflation data, and the variable to watch is the next meaningful shift in US real yields.

03 What moved it

Gold’s muted decline reflects the cross-currents of a slightly stronger dollar and still-firm US real yields, both of which raise the opportunity cost of holding a metal that does not pay interest, even as geopolitical tensions and doubts about the Federal Reserve’s next steps keep some safe-haven buyers in the market. In plain terms, investors weighing whether to hold gold or cash are seeing short-term US bonds yield around 4% or more, so only the most anxious or the most long-term inflation-focused buyers are adding to bullion positions at these levels.

Silver’s gain, by contrast, is easier to square with market psychology: investors attracted by its lower nominal price, its important role in clean energy technologies and its tendency to outperform gold in risk-on phases have been stepping back in after sharp falls, helped by expectations that mine supply growth will lag demand. Day-traders and more speculative funds often treat silver as a way to express views on both industrial growth and monetary fragility, so a session where the dollar is firm but not surging can still deliver a positive close for silver.

04 The Latin American read

Mexico’s position as the world’s leading silver producer, with around 6,300 metric tons of mine output in 2024, means that even a modest daily rise in silver prices has direct implications for local miners’ cash flows and for the country’s export revenues in a region where commodity cycles still matter deeply for currencies and equity markets. Peru, producing about 3,100 metric tons in 2024 and holding roughly 140,000 metric tons of silver reserves, is even more leveraged to longer-term price trends, as its vast in-ground resources make it a focal point for global investment in new projects and for debates about regulation and community consent.

For foreign investors scanning Latin America from abroad, the combination of a quietly rising silver price and concentrated production in Mexico and Peru underscores both opportunity and risk: higher prices can fatten margins at well-run mines, but they also sharpen local political debates over royalties, environmental oversight and who should benefit when the global system pays up for the region’s resources. In practical terms, the day’s tape is another reminder that silver is one of the clearest transmission channels between world markets and the balance sheets of Latin American governments and companies.

05 The names to watch

At the country level, the key names remain Mexico and Peru, which between them sit at the top of global silver production rankings and control a large share of known reserves, meaning that any shift in their tax regimes, permitting rules or community relations can ripple quickly through worldwide supply. On the corporate side, investors monitor both large diversified miners operating in the region and smaller silver-focused producers, including firms such as Silver X, which recently reported record quarterly production with silver-equivalent output rising more than 50% quarter-on-quarter, as bellwethers of how efficiently the sector is converting high-cost ore into saleable metal.

For a foreign reader, these names function as practical touchpoints: country data from institutions like the Silver Institute and Statista give the structural picture, while company reports show whether management teams are taking advantage of price moves or struggling with cost inflation and local politics. On days when silver prices rise while gold drifts, the performance gap between nimble producers and peers weighed down by operational or social issues can be wide, and that is where careful stock selection earns its keep.

06 The outlook

Looking ahead, the path for gold and silver will hinge on three linked questions: whether US inflation cools enough to ease pressure on real yields, whether the Federal Reserve signals a clear end to its tightening cycle and whether geopolitical risks flare up or fade, all of which feed directly into the appeal of dollar assets versus precious metals. If yields drift lower and the dollar softens, gold could regain some footing and silver may find stronger support from both industrial buyers and investors conscious of the concentration of supply in Mexico and Peru, but a renewed rise in yields or a sharper dollar rally would likely cap bullion and test the nerve of more speculative silver holders; the outlook, in other words, is balanced, and the variable to watch is the next decisive move in US real yields.

Dollar strength: Track the Dollar Index and key FX pairs because a stronger greenback makes gold and silver more expensive for non-US buyers and often weighs on prices despite safe-haven interest.

Frequently Asked Questions

Why did gold fall when risk feels high?

Gold tends to benefit from fear, but in this session higher real yields and a slightly stronger dollar raised the opportunity cost of holding bullion, offsetting safe-haven inflows and leaving the price only marginally lower rather than sharply higher.

Why did silver rise while gold barely moved?

Silver has a dual role as both industrial and monetary metal, so even when macro headwinds cap gold, investors can still buy silver on expectations of solid industrial demand and on the appeal of its lower nominal price and higher volatility.

How important are Mexico and Peru to silver?

Mexico is the largest silver producer with about 6,300 metric tons of output in 2024, while Peru produced around 3,100 metric tons and holds roughly 22% of known global silver reserves, making Latin America central to both current supply and future project pipelines.

What should a foreign investor focus on now?

Foreign investors should watch US real yields and the dollar to gauge the broad direction of gold, while following policy and corporate developments in Mexico and Peru to understand how silver supply risks and opportunities in Latin America might amplify or cushion global price moves.

04 The Latin American read

Latin America’s crypto story is still dominated by stablecoins, remittances and inflation hedging. One source says the region generated $324 billion in stablecoin transaction volume in 2025, and another says stablecoins account for nearly 40% of crypto purchases in the region.

The remittance angle matters most for readers outside the region: Latin America received $174 billion in remittances in 2025, and stablecoin transfers are being sold as cheaper than traditional money transfer channels. For countries such as Argentina and Brazil, where currency instability and cost pressures remain central, crypto is less a speculative theme than a practical dollar substitute.

Brazil matters because it is the region’s most important institutional market and one source says stablecoin transactions there are being brought under foreign-exchange-style rules from February 2026. That puts compliance, reporting and formal rails at the centre of adoption.

Argentina matters because inflation and capital controls have made crypto, especially stablecoins, a household tool rather than a novelty. El Salvador matters because it remains the symbolic Bitcoin case, even if the broader regional trend is now more about stablecoins than about everyday Bitcoin payments.

06 The outlook

The next phase in Latin America is likely to be shaped less by price thrills and more by whether stablecoins keep winning remittances, payroll and savings flows. If regulated access broadens in Brazil and cost advantages remain clear on routes into Argentina and El Salvador, crypto’s regional role should deepen rather than fade.

World.title: Historic UCR Music School Faces Possible Closure
World.content:
The historic building that houses the University of Costa Rica’s School of Musical Arts could lose its operating permit after health inspectors found infrastructure and sanitation problems, including openings that allow raccoons to enter the facility. The Ministry of Health gave the university until Monday, July 20, to comply with a sanitary order issued after an inspection in April. The order requires the university to address the building’s structural problems, eliminate areas where animals can shelter and improve waste-management practices.

Failure to comply could lead to penalties ranging from a temporary closure to the cancellation of the school’s sanitary operating permit. One of the most visible problems involves raccoons entering through openings near the building’s roof and exterior eaves. The animals have reportedly gained access to classrooms, offices and other interior spaces.

The School of Musical Arts has responded with cleaning and disinfection, more frequent garbage collection and efforts to seal entry points. However, administrators say those measures have reduced the problem without providing a permanent solution. University officials say the aging building requires broader structural work that the music school cannot complete with its own budget. The UCR rector’s office submitted a corrective plan to health authorities in June and requested additional time to carry out the repairs.

The university has said that concerns about the building’s condition were raised internally as early as 2023. Since then, the school has sought technical support and funding for repairs. The building contains classrooms, rehearsal rooms, administrative offices, a music library and spaces used for concerts and academic research. A closure would disrupt lessons, rehearsals and other activities while the university looks for temporary locations or completes the required work.

The School of Musical Arts is now waiting for the Ministry of Health to decide whether to approve the corrective plan and extend the deadline. No closure had been officially announced as of Monday morning.

World.title: Costa Rica Clears Legal Path for Recope to Move Beyond Petroleum
World.content:
Costa Rica’s Legislative Assembly has approved a reform that frees the state fuel company to work with energy sources other than oil for the first time, though drivers should not expect any immediate change in what they pay at the pump. Lawmakers gave final approval on July 16, to the Law to Promote the Energy Transition in the Fuel Sector, passing it in second debate with 54 votes in favor, none against and three legislators absent.

The bill had cleared its first debate two days earlier, capping an effort that had stalled repeatedly in the Assembly over more than a decade. It now goes to the executive branch for the president’s signature and publication before it can take effect. The reform rewrites the 1981 law governing the Refinadora Costarricense de Petróleo, or Recope, which until now was limited by statute to refining, transporting and selling petroleum and its derivatives.

Under the new framework, Recope keeps every one of those responsibilities but gains authority to research, acquire, import, export, process, store, transport and sell wholesale fuels derived from sources other than oil, with biofuels and green hydrogen named specifically. The law also brings natural gas within the company’s reach and broadens the mandate of the public services regulator, the Autoridad Reguladora de los Servicios Públicos, to cover the supply of gas, green hydrogen, biofuels, asphalts and naphthas.

Officials have stressed the limits of what the vote accomplishes. The measure works as a legal foundation rather than a finished project, and before Recope can enter any of these new markets it must present the Ministry of Environment and Energy, which sets national energy policy, with technical and operational studies showing that each step is warranted and consistent with that policy.

In the short term the law changes neither fuel prices nor the products available at service stations, and it does not mean green hydrogen or biofuels will go on sale anytime soon. To keep the reform from becoming a backdoor for fossil fuels, the text specifies that any Recope involvement in natural gas cannot be used to delay, replace or scale back investment in renewable energy.

Supporters frame the change as a matter of both economics and energy security. Costa Rica imports nearly all of the oil it burns, which leaves household budgets, business costs and public finances exposed to global price swings the country cannot control. That vulnerability stands in sharp contrast to the electricity sector, which drew 98.6 percent of its power from renewable sources in 2025, according to the Instituto Costarricense de Electricidad, after a two-year dip caused by drought. Even so, roughly 70 percent of the total energy the country consumes, transport fuel included, still comes from imported oil and gas, and that is the gap the reform is meant to begin closing.

The near-term consequence for drivers is a separate initiative that the new law reinforces but does not itself enact: the introduction of ethanol-blended gasoline. That plan, developed by the Ministry of Environment and Energy together with Recope, the services regulator and the University of Costa Rica, centers on an E10 blend, 10 percent ethanol mixed with 90 percent conventional fuel, the same standard sold across much of the United States. The blend would go first into premium gasoline, whose typically newer engines are designed to handle it, and Recope has already run pilot testing in the Pacific region to gauge both performance and public acceptance.

The timeline, however, has slipped. Authorities once aimed to have the blend reaching consumers by 2027, but the Ministry of Environment and Energy acknowledged in late June that the date is no longer assured. Recope must first make a series of purchases to produce the mixture, including sourcing the ethanol itself through an international tender that officials estimate will take about a year, and no firm calendar yet exists. Once the project’s implementing decrees are published, the company is expected to draw up a road map with clearer dates.

World.title: Costa Rica turned out for the 2026 World Cup final
World.content:
By early afternoon on Sunday, the concert grounds at Parque Metropolitano La Sabana had turned into an open-air stadium of their own. Families, groups of friends and visitors filled the space in front of a giant screen, faces painted, red Spanish shirts mixing with the sky blue and white of Argentina, waiting for a match that would crown a new world champion. When Ferran Torres struck in the second half of extra time, one half of the crowd erupted and the other fell quiet, and the afternoon tipped over into celebration.

Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time at the stadium in East Rutherford, New Jersey, to lift the trophy for the second time in the country’s history and the first since 2010. Torres, a substitute, scored the only goal in the 106th minute against an Argentine side reduced to ten men after Enzo Fernández was sent off late in regulation. For Lionel Messi, at 39, it was most likely a final World Cup appearance, and it ended without the trophy.

None of that happened in Costa Rica, and yet the country spent the day living it. San José was the center of it. The municipality turned La Sabana into the heart of its “San José Te Quiere Aquí” mid-year holiday festival, with the final shown free on a large screen, food markets, a craft fair and children’s activities across the weekend. National acts including Tapón and Luis Rosal warmed up the crowd, and the Colombian group Piso 21 closed the night with a free concert once the football was over. Organizers had projected space for a large capacity at the venue, and by kickoff the grounds were packed, though a confirmed attendance figure was not released.

The party was not limited to the capital. Municipalities set up fan zones with giant screens in Turrialba, at Parque Ignacio Pérez in Esparza, in Grecia and elsewhere, many of them pairing the broadcast with markets meant to draw people out and lift local business during the holiday week. Shopping centers joined in too, with venues such as Lincoln Plaza in Moravia installing screens for families who wanted somewhere to watch outside the house. For anyone who stayed home, the match aired free on Teletica and on subscription through FOX Sports and Tigo Sports, with kickoff at 1 p.m. local time.

The pull is easy to explain. This World Cup was co-hosted across the United States, Mexico and Canada, closer to Costa Rica than any tournament in memory, and it has been front of mind here for weeks even though the national team did not qualify. Costa Rica also has deep and personal ties to both finalists, through a large resident Spanish community and a steady Argentine presence, and both turned out. At La Sabana, dozens of Spanish fans, joined by Costa Ricans backing La Roja, celebrated the title with flags, hugs and chants once the final whistle blew. Argentine supporters, on the losing side, stayed to applaud their team and promised to be back for the next one.

That mix of heartbreak and pride played out on a far larger scale in Buenos Aires, where crowds gathered at the Obelisk with fireworks and flags to salute the runners-up, and where President Javier Milei said the squad could name a day to celebrate the second-place finish that would then be declared a national holiday. Coach Lionel Scaloni, who guided Argentina to the 2022 title, broke down in tears and cut short his post-match press conference, leaving his own future with the team an open question.

World.title: Miguelito Encalada gets two life sentences for murdering wife and brother
World.content:
Miguelito Encalada gets two life sentences for murdering wife and brother

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Miguelito Encalada was sentenced on Monday to two concurrent life sentences for the murders of his wife, Desiree Elizabeth Gonzalez, and his younger brother, George Vincent Rochester.

Justice Candace Nanton ordered that Encalada must serve at least 40 years before becoming eligible for parole. The sentences were backdated to April 24, 2023, when he was remanded to the Belize Central Prison.

Encalada was found guilty on May 22, 2026, of two counts of murder in connection with the fatal shootings, which occurred on April 20, 2023, at a restaurant and residence on Scissors Tail Street in the New Site area of Ladyville.

Justice Nanton began with a minimum term of 42 years, citing the use of a firearm, the close-range nature of the killings, the deaths of two close relatives and the fact that the murders occurred inside the victims’ home and business.

She deducted two years after considering Encalada’s good conduct while on remand, his completion of rehabilitation programmes, his lack of prison infractions and favourable accounts of his work mentoring young men in Ladyville and his role as a father.

Before being sentenced, Encalada offered condolences to both families but continued to maintain his innocence.

“I am not behind this crime. I am not the shooter,” he told the court, claiming the real killers remained in the community.

During his trial, Encalada said armed men entered the establishment, forced him to the ground and stole approximately $8,000. He claimed he later found Gonzalez and Rochester lying on the floor and denied having any involvement in their deaths.

Encalada was represented by attorney Hurl Hamilton, while Crown Counsel Glenfield Dennison appeared for the prosecution.

World.title: Juan Carlos Novelo acquitted of murdering common-law wife Leslie Verde
World.content:
Juan Carlos Novelo acquitted of murdering common-law wife Leslie Verde

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Juan Carlos Novelo was found not guilty on Monday of the November 2023 murder of his common-law wife, Leslie Margarita Verde, in Caye Caulker.

Justice Candace Nanton announced the verdict shortly before 2:40 p.m. on Monday, freeing Novelo of the murder charge. The judge said her reasons for the acquittal will be provided in a written decision at a later date.

“It feels good because I never killed my common-law wife,” Novelo said after leaving court. “I just want to say to the family, from my heart, I never did what they think I did. I am so happy with this verdict.”

Verde, a mother of two, was found motionless inside her home in the Bahia area of Caye Caulker during the early hours of November 4, 2023. She was taken to the Caye Caulker Health Clinic, where she was pronounced dead.

A post-mortem examination conducted by a doctor determined that Verde died from asphyxia caused by compression of the neck. He classified the death as a homicide, saying the injuries were not self-inflicted or accidental.

The prosecution’s case relied largely on circumstantial evidence, including surveillance footage showing Novelo entering and leaving Verde’s home around the time of her death.

Verde’s then-13-year-old daughter also testified that she awoke and saw Novelo shaking her mother’s motionless body. However, the child said she had been between sleeping and waking and later went back to sleep.

Novelo’s attorney, Leeroy Banner, argued that there were no eyewitnesses or reliable evidence proving that his client killed Verde. The defence maintained that Verde was alive when Novelo left the home and urged the court to acquit him.

World.title: Kenton Young critically injured in Belize River Valley shooting; two detained
World.content:
Kenton Young critically injured in Belize River Valley shooting; two detained

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police are investigating a shooting near the Mussel Creek Bridge that left 29-year-old Kenton Young of Bermudian Landing Village critically injured.

The shooting occurred at around 10:25 p.m. on Saturday, July 18, 2026.

Police said Young was travelling in his SUV when he was confronted by a man riding a motorcycle. The motorcyclist reportedly fired several shots at the vehicle, injuring Young.

Young was transported for medical treatment and was listed in a critical but stable condition at the time of the police briefing.

Investigators believe the shooting may be connected to an ongoing dispute involving individuals from Bermudian Landing and Lemonal villages. Two persons have been detained for questioning, while police are searching for a third individual.

Initial public reports described the incident as a shooting in the Burrell Boom area before police clarified that it occurred near Mussel Creek Bridge.

Young is also known within Belize’s cricket community and has previously been publicly identified as captain of the Belize National Cricket Team.

World.title: Santa Elena resident charged after police find four rounds of 9mm ammunition
World.content:
Santa Elena resident charged after police find four rounds of 9mm ammunition

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have arrested and charged 37-year-old Simon Bateman of Santa Elena Town with keeping ammunition without a gun licence.

Bateman’s arrest followed an intelligence-led operation conducted at his residence on Friday, July 17, 2026, as police searched for illegal firearms and ammunition.

Police said a search of Bateman’s person resulted in the discovery of four live rounds of 9mm ammunition.

Investigators determined that Bateman was not the holder of a gun license, and he was subsequently charged.

World.title: Bullet Tree Falls man charged after police allegedly find 9.2 grams of crack cocaine
World.content:
Bullet Tree Falls man charged after police allegedly find 9.2 grams of crack cocaine

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have arrested and charged 37-year-old Santos Ramirez of Bullet Tree Falls Village with possession of controlled drugs with intent to supply.

According to police, an officer was conducting patrols in Bullet Tree Falls on Thursday, July 16, 2026, when Ramirez’s behaviour reportedly aroused suspicion.

Ramirez was detained and searched. Police allege that the search resulted in the discovery of a bag containing suspected crack cocaine.

The substance was weighed and reportedly amounted to 9.2 grams. Ramirez was subsequently charged and taken before the court.

World.title: Criminal and internal investigations launched after off-duty cop shoots man in San Pedro during domestic disturbance
World.content:
Criminal and internal investigations launched after off-duty cop shoots man in San Pedro during domestic disturbance

By Breaking Belize News Staff: Police have launched simultaneous criminal and internal investigations after an off-duty police officer, identified as PC Keenan Yearwood shot Maverick Fuentes during an alleged domestic disturbance in San Pedro Town.

The incident occurred on Sunday, July 19, 2026, at an apartment building where the officer reportedly resides. Police said the officer was returning home when he encountered an ongoing domestic altercation in a common area of the building.

Police report that Yearwood reportedly attempted to de-escalate the situation, however, Fuentes’ common-law wife, Delia Martinez, claims that Yearwood entered their house without consent. Martinez claims Yearwood entered the home and attacked Fuentes, however, police report that Yearwood attempted to detain Fuentes but was attacked by both Fuentes and Martinez.

The officer then reportedly drew his personally licensed firearm and discharged one round, striking Fuentes in the leg. Martinez claims it was at this point that Yearwood called in for police backup, though police report that Yearwood had called for police assistance prior to entering the home.

Fuentes was airlifted from the island for further medical treatment. According to Martinez, Fuentes suffered a broken leg due to the gunshot. The officer also sought medical attention, though the extent of his injuries has not been disclosed.

Police have confiscated the Yearwood’s firearm and recovered the expended shell casing. Martinez also told Breaking Belize News that during the scuffle, Yearwood dropped a fully loaded magazine, which she later found and turned in to CIB.

No charges have been brought against anyone at this stage as investigators work to establish the full sequence of events and obtain statements from the woman and other potential witnesses.

World.title: International News: Ortega says Nicaragua will no longer hold elections
World.content:
International News: Ortega says Nicaragua will no longer hold elections

By Zoila Palma: Nicaraguan President Daniel Ortega has announced that the country will no longer hold elections, a move that would eliminate the possibility of an electoral challenge when his current term ends and further consolidate the power he shares with his wife, Vice President Rosario Murillo.

Ortega, who has remained in power since 2007 after previously serving as president in the 1980s, said the decision would close the door to any opposition takeover.

However, he did not provide specific details on how the change would be implemented or what political system would replace the electoral process, Reuters report.

The announcement comes amid growing international criticism of Ortega and Murillo’s government.

The United Nations Human Rights Council has accused Nicaragua’s leadership of transforming the country into an authoritarian state and carrying out systematic human rights violations.

World.title: International News: Australian woman gives birth to rare identical quadruplets
World.content:
International News: Australian woman gives birth to rare identical quadruplets

By Zoila Palma: An Australian couple is celebrating the birth of four identical baby girls after an extremely rare, naturally conceived pregnancy that doctors estimate occurs in only one out of every 15 million pregnancies.

The babies were delivered by caesarean section at 28 weeks and four days on July 14 at the Royal Brisbane and Women’s Hospital, BBC reports.

The newborns — Emily, Harriet, Catherine and Alexa — are monozygotic quadruplets, meaning they developed after a single fertilized egg split into four embryos. Doctors described the pregnancy as exceptionally high-risk, with the babies sharing one placenta, a condition specialists said is virtually unheard of.

Doctors closely monitored 34-year-old mother Jenitar Na’amoana after admitting her to the hospital at 25 weeks. Maternal fetal medicine specialist Dr. Alexa Bendall said reaching 28 weeks was a major milestone, adding that both the mother and babies avoided the serious complications often associated with such pregnancies. The fourth baby was named Alexa in honor of the doctor.

The four girls are receiving care in the hospital’s neonatal intensive care unit and are reported to be doing well.

World.title: Jamaica received more than 1,300 deportees in 2025, says PIOJ
World.content:
The majority of the deportees, also referred to as involuntary returned migrants (IRMs), came from the United States.

The survey also found that the total number of voluntary returned migrants (VRMs) stood at 852 in 2025, an increase of 52.1 per cent when compared with the 560 who returned home in 2024.

VRMs are individuals who choose to return to their home country or place of origin due to personal decisions, economic opportunities or family reasons.

Conversely, IRMs are those who are forcibly returned or repatriated to their country of origin due to legal reasons such as immigration violations or criminal activities.

In the meantime, the number of Commonwealth Citizens who migrated to Jamaica in 2025 decreased by 3.8 per cent to 3,491 from 3,630 in 2024.

The PIOJ said there was also an increase in the number of aliens registered in 2025, with the figure jumping to 11,029 when compared to the 2024 figure, which stood at 10,146, an 8.7 per cent increase.

The planning institute said that at 49.0 per cent, Asians accounted for the largest share of individuals who requested extension of stay beyond six months, followed by Caribbean nationals at 19.4 per cent, and Africans at 11.4 per cent.

World.title: 27 dead, 83 missing from capsized Guyana ferry, says PM
World.content:
Handout picture released by NCN Guyana showing President Irfaan Ali (L) attending a meeting with some of the survivors and relatives of those still missing after a ferry carrying more than 100 people capsized off the coast of the country, in Mabaruma, Region One, Guyana, on July 20, 2026. The ageing ferry MV Barima capsized off the coast of Guyana late on July 18 during a trip from the capital Georgetown to Port Kaituma. Rescue teams saved 67 people, officials said, as the search continues into July 20. (Photo by Handout / NCN Guyana / AFP)

GEORGETOWN, Guyana (AFP) — At least 27 people died after a ferry capsized off the coast of Guyana, Prime Minister Mark Phillips said Monday, as the small South American nation mourned the tragedy.

Sixty-nine people aboard the MV Barima have been rescued since the vessel flipped over on Saturday night, Phillips told reporters, adding that 83 more remained missing.

“Our focus again is on finding people,” he said, having raised the death toll from a previous 10. “We still have hope.”

READ: Death toll rises as more bodies found following boating tragedy

The aging ferry was traveling from the capital Georgetown to Guyana’s inland Essequibo region when it overturned.

Phillips said he was now “confident” that 179 people were aboard, following uncertainty about the numbers involved in the disaster.

Public Works Minister Juan Edghill earlier stated that the ship’s passenger manifest listing 133 people on board was inaccurate.

Authorities earlier Monday expanded the size of the area being searched from 400 to 1,070 square kilometers (154 to 413 square miles), while local fishermen joined recovery efforts.

The French army also sent 12 divers, two doctors and a mechanic from nearby French Guiana to aid the search-and-rescue operation, the presidency said.

Two crewmembers aboard the aging ferry tested positive for marijuana after the incident, Phillips had told reporters Sunday, adding that an investigation was underway.

The ship began its journey in mid-afternoon and a distress call was received about eight hours later, Edghill earlier said.

The ferry was built in 1939, according to the shipping website VesselFinder.

Boats typically travel by sea before reaching a river to arrive at Port Kaituma, which is located in the depths of a dense rainforest.

World.title: WATCH: A colourful goodbye to late revival singer Kukudoo
World.content:
KINGSTON, Jamaica – A vibrant celebration of life unfolded Sunday as scores of mourners gathered at the Ranny Williams Entertainment Centre in St Andrew to bid farewell to late gospel and revival singer David “Kukudoo” McDermott.

McDermott died on May 8 after a battle with cancer. He was 52.

In a fitting farewell on Sunday, his funeral was marked by colourful traditions, spirited dancing and soul-stirring songs.

There were also glowing tributes from members of the gospel music fraternity, friends, family and government officials including Entertainment and Culture Minister Olivia Grange; State Minister in the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Foreign Trade, Arlando Terrelonge; and State Minister in the Ministry of Health and Wellness, Krystal Lee.

McDermott’s remains were interred at the Dovecot Memorial Park.

(Video by Llewellyn Wynter)

World.title: More traffic headache coming for motorists in Liguanea
World.content:
Sewer upgrade work underway on Retreat Avenue off Old Hope Road on Saturday. The work will shortly be extended on Old Hope Road to its intersection with Wellington Drive. Naphtali Junior

MOTORISTS in the Liguanea area of St Andrew should brace for major traffic disruptions this summer as the National Water Commission (NWC) undertakes the renovation of sewage infrastructure along Old Hope Road

Speaking during a recent meeting of the Jamaica Observer Press Club at the newspaper’s headquarters in St Andrew, Minister of Water Matthew Samuda said the work forms part of the Government’s ongoing programme to strengthen resilience through upgrading the county’s water and sewage network.

He explained that work on Munroe Road and Wellington Drive, which led to traffic snarls in the area for weeks, is now complete, allowing work to begin on the stretch of Old Hope Road that runs through Liguanea, Matilda’s Corner, and Seymour Avenue.

Samuda told Observer editors and reporters that work along that corridor was deliberately postponed to avoid disrupting students travelling to sit their various examinations.

“We didn’t start last month because we didn’t want to run the risk of a child being stuck in traffic trying to get to their PEP [Primary Exit Profile] exams at St Peter and Paul, or a child trying to get to Campion to do their CXC [Caribbean Examination Council] exams along that particular space. We expect to start in the coming week or so,” said the minister.

World.title: APOLOGY AND CORRECTION
World.content:
Dayton Campbell

On Monday, 13 July 2026, the Jamaica Observer published an article entitled ‘Dead girl’s ghost haunts Dayton’.

The Observer acknowledges that the headline was capable of conveying the false impression that Dr Campbell had some association with, or responsibility for, the rape and murder of Diane Smith. The Observer acknowledges that any such implication is entirely false.

Dr Campbell was an infant when Diane Smith was raped and murdered. He has never been implicated, suspected, or connected in any way with that tragic crime.

The Observer further acknowledges that Dr Campbell did not repeat or endorse any allegation connecting any person to the rape and murder of Diane Smith, whether debunked or otherwise.

The Jamaica Observer sincerely apologises to Dr Campbell for the distress, embarrassment, and reputational harm occasioned by the publication and withdraws any defamatory imputations arising therefrom.

World.title: Puzzling double murder in Mandeville
World.content:
An undated photo of murder victim Deneekia Pounall, 24, Knox Community College nursing student and resident of Heartease district in Manchester .

MANDEVILLE, Manchester — Even as police here have launched a manhunt for a gunman who posed as a passenger in a taxi before disembarking the vehicle and killing two passengers on Saturday, detectives are struggling to make sense of the incident as up to press time they had not determined a motive for the attack.

“It is senseless…He paid his fare and got his change and the vehicle drove off and he just fired shots on it. The motive is not clear, because why would you shoot up a vehicle with seven people,” a senior police source told the Jamaica Observer on Sunday.

Police identified those killed as Deneekia Pounall, 24, a nursing student at Knox Community College, a resident of Heartease in the parish, and her neighbour 21-year-old Sadefa Henry.

According to the police, about 7:30 pm on Saturday, Pounall and Henry were seated in a Toyota Voxy operated as a public passenger vehicle on the Mandeville to Royal Flat route when a man, who was a passenger in the vehicle, disembarked at a section of Caledonia Road commonly referred to as Horseshoe Curve.

The man reportedly opened fire on the seven occupants of the taxi, hitting the two who were seated at the back of the vehicle.

They were taken to the Mandeville Regional Hospital where Pounall was pronounced dead on arrival, while Henry later succumbed to his injuries.

Residents of Heartease told the

Observer on Sunday that Pounall and Henry lived in neighbouring apartments at a property in the community.

“She was such a calm girl. She nuh talk, and the guy was quiet and humble, so this incident is quite puzzling,” said a resident who requested anonymity.

The double murder has increased the number of homicides reported in Manchester to 20 since the start of the year.

Just last week acting head of the police’s Area Three, Senior Superintendent Shane McCalla, predicted that fewer than 94 murders will be recorded across Manchester, Clarendon, and St Elizabeth by year end, following the launch of Operation Reset last month.

“We are trending upwards in the murder and aggravated assaults, so Operation Reset was primarily designed to address this…and in terms of the acquisitive crimes, we are trending down by 104. This is our commitment to the High Command that Area Three will deliver in December,” he told the Jamaica Constabulary Force’s High Command last Wednesday at the Mandeville police station.

McCalla gave a breakdown of murders statistics down the years in Area Three. He said in 2023 there were 189 murders, in 2024 there were 150 murders, while 94 murders were recorded last year.

“Year to date we have 58 [murders]. Despite seeing some issues where St Elizabeth is concerned… I am convinced and I am committing to you that we will end under the 94 [in December],” he vowed.

World.title: Sumfest history
World.content:
Mavado (left) and Vybz Kartel share the Sumfest stage. (Garfield Robinson)

For 18 years it remained one of dancehall’s biggest unanswered questions: Could the music that once divided a nation ever become the force that united it?

Shortly after 2:00 am on Sunday that question was answered inside Plantation Cove as a Taste of Reggae Sumfest delivered an experience of history-making proportions.

Vybz Kartel and Mavado stood shoulder to shoulder on the festival’s grand stage, writing a new chapter in one of the most defining narratives in dancehall culture. The showdown was far more than an exhibition of hit songs. It was the closing of a circle that began during the combative Gully/Gaza era — a rivalry that shaped an entire generation of dancehall fans and forever altered the genre’s landscape.

Dressed for battle, but performing in brotherhood, both deejays were ready to give fans exactly what they asked for.

Without hesitation, they reached back into the catalogue that made them icons. Serving up songs such as

The Real McKoy, Real Deal, Send A Hell, the entertainers elicited loud cheers of approval from the sold-out crowd.

The tension that once defined the rivalry had given way to celebration.

“This a history innu,” Mavado declared.

“Memba dat,” Kartel responded before embracing his long-time rival.

“We ago gi unnu supm unnu never see yet,” Kartel continued.

For two hours they spewed hit after hit from their arsenal of songs.

For Professor Donna Hope, one of Jamaica’s foremost authorities on dancehall culture, the significance of the moment extended well beyond nostalgia.

“Eighteen years later… We have been through many things, they’ve been in exile in different ways, they lost things, they gained things, and so the energy was different,” she reflected after the performance. “Gaza/Gully in 2008 was a very combative energy but Reggae Sumfest 2026, it was different. Their performance reminded people that dancehall culture is alive and well and Vybz Kartel and Mavado are powerful artistes that have matured and now understand the mission and are carrying it out.”

Even while revisiting songs born from lyrical warfare, the two men frequently completed each other’s lyrics, laughed together, and embraced the shared legacy they helped create. Records that once encouraged fans to choose sides became reminders of just how deeply both artistes have shaped modern dancehall.

Mavado confidently held his own with crowd favourites, including Weh Dem A Do, Top Shatta Nah Miss, Chat Too Much, Warn Dem, and Amazing Grace.

Kartel answered with equal force, unleashing anthem after anthem through Gaza Army, Broad Daylight, Kill Dem All, Done, Weh Dem A Go, Murder Informa, and Never Scared.

Female fans were delighted with selections including Love Dem, Picture Me & You, Beg You (A Touch), and Come Home, while Mavado countered with Squeeze Breast, Bicycle, Ever Blessed, When You Feel Lonely, and Never Believe You.

The surprises continued as Mavado invited Stacious to recreate their hit Come Into My Room, while Kartel called on Gaza Hindu to perform Spice’s verses on Ramping Shop and Virginity.

“It’s a good feeling to be back on a Sumfest stage,” said Stacious. “Tonight I’m here not just as an artiste, but as a fan of dancehall who lived through the era where Gully/Gaza did a run road… Mavado hasn’t performed in Jamaica for a while so I was happy to witness that return and be a part of it… [I]t’s always fun when we connect…” As they got ready to draw the curtains on their historic set, the clash songs and romance anthems gave way to messages of gratitude and faith as the deejays delivered Hope and Pray, God Is the Greatest, The Messiah, and Thank Yuh Jah. Then came the perfect ending. Their first collaboration, Happiest Days. “This a the first song me and him ever do,” Kartel reminded the audience. “Listen to it good and see how everything come full circle.” Few closing songs could carry greater symbolism — history, legacy secured!

World.title: Germany’s Merz turns resignation of party bigwig to his advantage
World.content:
The reshuffle is attractive to Merz because Spahn was sometimes an obstacle to him: The 46-year-old former health minister was not only an internal party rival who at times pushed back against his plans, but was also disliked by the more left-wing politicians amid his coalition partners in the Social Democratic Party (SPD).

With Spahn gone, Merz can choose a new CDU parliamentary leader to settle down the coalition. A cabinet reshuffle also allows him to make a political reset before crucial regional elections in the fall, in which the far-right Alternative for Germany (AfD) party is expected to perform well and could even secure an absolute majority in the eastern German state of Saxony-Anhalt in September.

Merz’s spokesman Stefan Kornelius said the chancellor was now weighing his next move.

“There are always possibilities — that is, they exist, or they are seized upon, or they are not seized upon — and once a decision has been made, I think [the chancellor] will let us know,” Kornelius told reporters. “The process is underway.”

Merz and fellow high-ranking conservatives are expected to come up with a concrete proposal over the coming days.

Following a CDU leadership meeting on Monday, conservative lawmakers were asked to prepare for a gathering in the Bundestag on Wednesday next week — despite the ongoing summer recess — to elect a new parliamentary group leader, according to a message sent to lawmakers and seen by POLITICO.

World.title: What Andy Burnham’s new-look Cabinet tells us about Britain’s direction
World.content:
Here’s who’s up, who’s down and who’s made a lateral move.

The winners

The biggest surprise was John Healey becoming chancellor. The second-most-important job in government was a big reward for the MP whose resignation as defense secretary a little over five weeks ago ensured there could be no chance of Starmer fighting on.

Healey will insist that he quit purely on principle over how the Starmer administration was failing to sufficiently increase defense spending in a perilous world. But that resignation also came with a barb about the “unwilling” Treasury he now commands.

Angela Rayner, who is the new housing secretary, rings the doorbell as she arrives at No. 10 Downing St. in London on July 20, 2026. | Dan Kitwood/Getty Images

He will have to fill the multi-billion-pound holes in government spreadsheets created by the Defence Investment Plan that was ultimately agreed after he quit, and work out how to facilitate the major hike in defense spending to 3 percent of GDP by 2030, as he demanded. To tax more or to cut existing budgets? That is the question.

For now, he will be seen as a safe pair of hands with experience across government, including in the Treasury back in Tony Blair’s administration in the 2000s. Burnham will hope he’s sufficiently safe not to spook the bond markets, which have at times been jittery about the prospect of this new PM.

One No. 10 official insisted Burnham and Healey have the “same outlook” when it comes to re-industrialization, devolution and the cost of living — key planks of Burnham’s plans — as well as the need to stick with the government’s “fiscal rules” aimed at securing economic stability.

World.title: Wes Streeting named to top UK defense role
World.content:
Wes Streeting arrives at Downing Street on July 20, 2026 before he was named defense secretary in the new Burnham Cabinet. | Ryan Jenkinson/Getty Images

The former health secretary had initially intended to challenge Keir Starmer but now joins Burnham’s cabinet.

LONDON — Wes Streeting will become the U.K.’s new defense secretary, Downing Street announced, as Andy Burnham unveiled his new Cabinet after becoming prime minister.

Streeting take over less than six weeks after predecessor Dan Jarvis, who was appointed amid a fierce row within government over defense spending, was named to the job by Burnham's predecessor Keir Starmer.

Jarvis was responsible for delivering the government’s long-awaited Defence Investment Plan, which allocated money to the capabilities needed to deal with the biggest threats to the U.K. over the next four years.

World.title: Britain’s Brexit Minister Nick Thomas-Symonds axed in reshuffle
World.content:
As Cabinet Office minister, Thomas-Symonds also had responsibility for other policy areas including public inquiries and civil service reform.

His departure comes at a key time for negotiations between Britain and the EU.

Before Starmer’s resignation, a U.K.-EU summit had been scheduled for Wednesday July 22 to round off talks on issues like an agri-food agreement, youth mobility scheme, and emissions trading deal.

Starmer had also planned to use the meeting as a launchpad for a closer relationship with the bloc.

The meeting was postponed upon Starmer’s resignation and is now expected to be rescheduled for later this year — with a new minister in charge on the British side.

“I hope that you will continue the negotiations I have started for U.K. participation in the EU's internal electricity market, and implement the key pillars of the Common Understanding: the food and drink agreement; the linking of the U.K. and EU Emissions Trading Systems; and the Youth Experience Scheme that will provide opportunities for young people to travel, work and study across Europe,” Thomas-Symonds wrote in his letter.

World.title: EU bets fossil fuel lobby is crying wolf over supply shock warnings
World.content:
Instead, it has issued new guidelines advising EU countries’ governments to hold off on fining offenders for three years. While that doesn’t officially remove the requirements, it would suspend enforcement to give companies more time to comply. The guidelines, first reported by POLITICO, were made official Monday after months of speculation. Member countries will discuss them Wednesday.

The Commission’s gamble is that companies are raking in so much money from selling to Europe — especially as the closure of the Strait of Hormuz sends energy prices soaring — that they won’t kill a lucrative trade just because of some legal uncertainties.

The executive is also confident that compliance won’t be a problem in the first place, and has reassured diplomats that its three-year “grace period” for penalties will stand up in court if member countries implement it properly. Last week it issued further guidance to help companies prove the emissions intensity of cargoes — a key detail they say has been missing.

“People will come to their senses” over the summer, said one EU official, granted anonymity to speak openly. The guidelines “will make it clearer how and when to comply, and it will become clearer that most importers can comply and will comply rather than lose their sales in a liquid global gas market.”

It’s true that business is booming for companies exporting to Europe. In the first 100 days after the U.S. and Israel’s attack on Iran, the EU paid an additional €62 billion for energy supplies, according to the Jacques Delors Institute. In particular, the bloc massively increased its imports of jet fuel and liquefied natural gas from the U.S., one of the most vocal opponents of the methane rules.

The conviction that companies won’t abandon Europe was illustrated in a meeting of EU ambassadors last week, during which the Commission told member countries that it would be best to wait until 2028 to assess the impact of the rules, instead of tearing them open on the basis of industry speculation, according to two diplomats briefed on the meeting.

World.title: Inquiet des usages de l’IA par les députés, le Parlement européen a une solution
World.content:
“Le Parlement n’a pas été épargné par les erreurs liées à l’IA et les contenus trompeurs générés par IA”, a observé Brando Benifei, député européen du groupe des Socialistes et démocrates qui a dirigé les travaux du Parlement sur l’AI Act, la législation phare de l’UE encadrant cette technologie. “Les députés européens doivent montrer l’exemple à mesure que les règles de transparence prévues par l’AI Act entrent en vigueur.”

Ce projet met en lumière le dilemme auquel est confronté le Parlement à mesure que l’IA générative s’intègre dans son travail. Quelque 2 100 personnes utilisent quotidiennement l’IA, soit environ 20% de l’ensemble des effectifs.

Ses dirigeants souhaitent que les responsables publics cessent de mettre des documents parlementaires sur des plateformes publiques non contrôlées, mais ils craignent également que cette technologie ne nuise à la qualité du travail législatif et n’introduise des erreurs ou des contenus trompeurs dans le processus démocratique. Ils ont soupçonné que les parlementaires et leurs assistants utilisaient déjà l’IA après une recrudescence d’amendements nécessitant une traduction, des styles de rédaction révélateurs et des références parfois fantaisistes à des lois qui n’existent pas.

Les présidents des commissions ont demandé au secrétaire général du Parlement, Alessandro Chiocchetti, d’élaborer des lignes directrices concernant l’utilisation de l’IA par les parlementaires. Celui-ci a répondu que cette question pourrait plutôt relever de la commission des Affaires constitutionnelles, qui devrait alors modifier le règlement intérieur de l’institution afin d’introduire des règles plus strictes.

Aujourd’hui, les députés européens ne sont pas tenus d’indiquer si leurs amendements, questions ou autres travaux parlementaires ont été élaborés à l’aide de l’intelligence artificielle.

Barry Andrews, président Renew de la commission du Développement, a affirmé qu’il était déjà évident que certains députés européens utilisaient l’intelligence artificielle pour rédiger des questions parlementaires, des discours et des amendements.

World.title: EU hits China’s Alibaba with €550M record fine over illegal products
World.content:
The finding that AliExpress failed to check and tackle these risks "is very dangerous for our consumers, but it’s also unfair for those companies that are complying with all our rules," Virkkunen said.

The record fine is the third one imposed under the Digital Services Act so far. It comes two months after Brussels hit rival marketplace Temu with a €200 million bill over similar breaches. “We were looking at the duration and the seriousness of these failures when deciding the size of the fine," Virkkunen said, recalling that Temu had so far only been sanctioned for failing to check its service for illegal products sold in Europe properly.

The Commission opened a probe into AliExpress in March 2024 over suspected breaches of the DSA, including also on the platform's transparency on advertising and recommender systems. Many of these suspected breaches were already settled in a series of commitments in June 2025.

In its new findings, the EU assessed that AliExpress failed to "evaluate whether it had sufficient staff to review potentially illegal products," leading to "overcharged" moderators having "only like 10 or 20 seconds to review the illegal product," a senior Commission official said in a briefing ahead of the announcement. It also failed to assess how its recommender and advertising systems "exacerbate" the spread of illegal products and relied on compliance checks that "could easily be circumvented through mis-categorization."

AliExpress has until Oct. 20 to come up with an "action plan" to address the infringements, which lasted at least until June 2025, or face additional penalties.

A spokesperson for AliExpress said in a statement that the company will appeal the EU's decision, calling it a "disproportionate fine [which] ignores our sound risk management framework and the significant, proactive enhancements we have made." They added: "AliExpress has been and continues to be committed to meeting our obligations to consumers."

This article was updated to include a comment from AliExpress confirming it will appeal the decision.

World.title: More than a million fans fill Madrid’s streets to welcome world champions
World.content:
World Cup champions Spain began their open-top bus parade through the streets of Madrid on Monday evening, as more than one million fans turned out to celebrate.

 

The victory parade is making its way through the Spanish capital, where thousands of supporters are greeting the team with chants of "España, España" and a sea of mobile phones held aloft to capture the moment.

Supporters pack Madrid’s streets

Hundreds of thousands of supporters filled the streets of Madrid on Monday to celebrate Spain’s World Cup victory with the national team.

According to the Government Delegation, more than one million people lined the route of the team’s open-top bus through the city centre cheering the players.

From the bus, the players waved to the crowds, lifted the World Cup trophy and celebrated with supporters lining the streets.

The capital has turned red and white to welcome the Spanish team, with thousands of supporters filling the streets, the Metro stations and the bus route.

Thousands of supporters turn Cibeles Square red as they welcome the world champions after their victory over Argentina. Selección Española Masculina de Fútbol

The tension of the final is now behind them, replaced by emotion and an overwhelming desire to celebrate a new world title.

Pedro Sánchez pays tribute to Spain's world champions

Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez welcomed Spain's national team to on Monday to celebrate their World Cup triumph.

The Prime Minister thanked the players and coaching staff for their efforts and the football they produced throughout the tournament, before urging them to dream of another title in 2030.

"Why not believe that, as the saying goes, good things come in threes?" he said.

Official reception with Spain’s royal family

Spain’s national team was received at Zarzuela Palace by King Felipe VI and Queen Letizia, accompanied by Princess Leonor and Infanta Sofía, following their World Cup triumph.

During the ceremony, the players broke into the traditional chant of “Campeones, campeones” before posing for the official photograph. The King hailed the victory as an “epic triumph” and thanked the team for returning Spain to the summit of world football.

He also praised the team’s efforts throughout the tournament and dismissed the criticism it had faced, insisting that nothing could overshadow “the joy of bringing the trophy home”.

La Roja in Madrid

Spain’s national team is now back in Madrid. The Iberia flight bringing them home from the United States landed at Adolfo Suárez Madrid-Barajas Airport.

Before the official World Cup celebrations got under way, the players had a few hours’ rest to celebrate the triumph with their families.

This is the first time the team has set foot on Spanish soil since lifting the World Cup, 16 years after their historic triumph at the 2010 tournament in South Africa.

The Spanish capital has turned red to welcome the new champions on a route that will culminate in Cibeles Square, where the main celebrations for Spain's second World Cup title will take place.

FIFA opens disciplinary proceedings against Argentina

FIFA has opened disciplinary proceedings against Argentina over incidents involving several players and a member of the coaching staff during the World Cup final.

The governing body will investigate their conduct and determine whether any sanctions should be imposed.

World.title: Chess legend Judit Polgar rejects offer to become Hungary's president
World.content:
Chess legend Judit Polgar on Monday turned down Hungarian Prime Minister Peter Magyar's offer to become the country's next president.

 

"I do not feel I have the strength to take on the historic responsibility of uniting a divided nation, and so I am unable to accept the invitation," Polgar posted on social media.

"I will do everything in my power to support a new, independent, and respected President of the Republic in achieving these goals," she added.

Polgar issued her response after the Tisza parliamentary group publicly backed her in parliament. However, critics noted that, contrary to earlier promises, her nomination was not preceded by broad public consultation.

Magyar responded to Polgar's decision in a comment.

"Dear Judit, thank you for everything you have done for Hungary. I believe I can say, on behalf of millions of Hungarians, that even if in a different capacity, we will continue to count on you in the future," he wrote.

After ejecting unpopular President Tamas Sulyok by constitutional amendment last week, Magyar backed Polgar late on Sunday as "a president of whom all Hungarians can be proud".

As a result of the constitutional amendment, current President Tamás Sulyok's mandate ended on Monday.

Leaders of the governing Tisza party have repeatedly said they want the president to be elected directly by the public rather than by parliament. As a result, the president elected now could serve only temporarily, until a new constitution is adopted.
